texts.astra.yaml:
# ASTRA Analysis Specification
# Documentation: https://github.com/LightconeResearch/ASTRA
#
# UNIONS-3500 Paper II, B-mode validation (Daley et al. 2026): pure-mode, COSEBI
# and harmonic-space null tests of the ShapePipe v1.4 catalogs, from the catalogs
# to each reported figure, table and finding.

version: "0.0.14"
name: "UNIONS-3500 B-mode Validation"
description: |
  B-mode null tests of the UNIONS-3500 ShapePipe v1.4 shear catalogs (Daley et
  al. 2026). Pure-mode correlation functions, COSEBIs and harmonic-space power
  spectra, with covariances validated on GLASS mocks, inform
  the fiducial catalog and scale cuts of the UNIONS cosmology papers.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Top-level inputs: what came from outside this analysis, the catalogs of Paper I,
# the n(z) and the survey areas.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
inputs:
  - id: shapepipe_v14_catalogs
    type: data
    description: |
      ShapePipe v1.4 cosmic-shear catalogs from Paper I
      (Hervas-Peters et al. 2026, Table H.1). Four variants enter the
      null tests:
      initial (size cut r_h,gal/r_h,psf > 0.5), size-cut (> 0.707;
      fiducial), masked (size-cut plus stellar-halo masking, 13%
      area loss) and relaxed-flags (size-cut with relaxed
      SExtractor deblending flags, +26% n_eff). Each comes with and
      without the object-wise PSF-leakage correction; the corrected
      versions are fiducial. A fifth, v1.4.6, is the footprint of the
      [published GLASS suite](#decisions.mock_suite). The files are the
      released cut catalogs at
      `vos:cfis/weak_lensing/ShapePipe/v1.4.x/v{version}/`;
      `src/cosmo_val/cat_config.yaml` holds every null-test variant's path.
    source: "data/v1.4.x/v{version}/unions_shapepipe_cut_struc_2024_v{version}.fits"

  - id: redshift_distributions
    type: data
    description: |
      The fiducial catalog's SOM-calibrated photometric n(z), one per
      blind (A / B / C). Every catalog version uses it: the n(z) enters
      theory and covariances, never the measured data vectors, and the
      B-mode covariance
      of a null signal is shape noise in configuration space and moves
      by under 0.5% between n(z) in harmonic space
      ([bmode_null_tests_insensitive_to_blinding](#findings.bmode_null_tests_insensitive_to_blinding)).
    source: "data/nz/nz_SP_v1.4.6.3_{blind}.txt"

  - id: survey_areas
    type: data
    description: |
      The survey area of each catalog, in deg²: 2894.03 for every
      variant but the masked one (2517.02). The values are Paper I's,
      measured on a high-resolution HEALPix footprint that combines the
      structural masks with a binned comprehensive catalog, which
      cannot be remade from the catalogs here. They set the area of
      every CosmoCov covariance and of every quoted density. The
      galaxies occupy 3–5% less (2750.65 deg² for the fiducial catalog
      at nside 4096, from the
      [catalog summary](#analyses.catalog_processing.outputs.catalog_summary)),
      so the area is a convention, shared with Papers III and IV.
    source: "data/survey_areas.yaml"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Top-level outputs: every figure, table and metric the report shows or the
# findings cite, re-exported from the sub-analysis that computes it. Figures run
# in the paper's order.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
outputs:
  # The B-mode data vectors of the fiducial catalog, each in units of its
  # uncertainty: pure E/B ξ±, COSEBI B_n (full range over the fiducial cut; the
  # >4σ first mode at full range is the visible evidence behind
  # `ccd_scale_cosebi_pattern`), and Cℓ^BB with Cℓ^EB.
  - {id: fig_pure_eb_decomposition, from: significance.pure_eb_data_vector_figure}
  - {id: fig_cosebis_fiducial, from: significance.cosebis_data_vector_figure}
  - {id: fig_cl_fiducial, from: significance.cl_data_vector_figure}

  # The pure E/B covariance, and the mock validation of estimators and
  # covariances that licenses it.
  - {id: fig_eb_covariance, from: covariances.pure_eb_covariance_figure}
  - {id: fig_mock_validation, from: validation.mock_validation_figure}
  - {id: fig_mock_min_pte, from: significance.mock_min_pte_figure}

  # The four catalog variants compared: pure-mode ξ_±^B, Cℓ^BB, COSEBI B_n.
  - {id: fig_versions_pure_eb, from: significance.pure_eb_version_comparison_figure}
  - {id: fig_versions_cl, from: significance.cl_version_comparison_figure}
  - {id: fig_versions_cosebis, from: significance.cosebis_version_comparison_figure}

  # PTEs over every scale-cut pair, configuration and harmonic space.
  - {id: fig_pte_heatmaps, from: significance.pte_heatmaps_figure}
  - {id: fig_cl_pte_heatmap, from: significance.cl_pte_heatmap_figure}

  # COSEBIs from harmonic bandpowers against those from ξ±.
  - {id: fig_harmonic_config_cosebis_full, from: validation.cosebis_harmonic_figure}

  # The blind-independence check behind the single-blind choice.
  - {id: bb_covariance_blind_independence_evidence, from: validation.bb_covariance_blind_independence_evidence}

  # Headline PTE table.
  - {id: pte_table_appendix, from: significance.pte_table_appendix}

  # Supporting data products cited by the report's inline macros and findings
  # (type: data, so Studio shows them under Data rather than Results).
  - {id: paper_claims, from: significance.paper_claims}
  - {id: mock_min_pte_calibration, from: significance.mock_min_pte_calibration}
  - {id: cosebis_first_mode_significance, from: significance.cosebis_first_mode_significance}
  - {id: nu_penalty_verdicts, from: significance.nu_penalty_verdicts}
  - {id: cosebis_harmonic_config, from: significance.cosebis_harmonic_config}
  - {id: mock_campaign_evidence, from: validation.mock_campaign_evidence}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Top-level decisions: the choices shared across the analysis (catalog,
# cosmology, scale cuts, blind, pure-mode estimator, PTE conventions), which
# sub-analyses inherit via `from: ../<id>`.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
decisions:

  fiducial_catalog:
    label: "Fiducial catalog variant"
    tags: [data_selection]
    rationale: |
      Which ShapePipe v1.4 variant the reported results rest on.
      The size-cut catalog is adopted because tightening the
      galaxy-to-PSF size cut removes the ξ_-^B and Cℓ^BB failures of
      the initial catalog, and it is the only variant that passes
      every statistic at the fiducial cuts
      ([finding](#findings.only_size_cut_catalog_passes),
      [PTE table](#outputs.pte_table_appendix)). The masked and
      relaxed-flags variants are compared alongside it. All four are
      leakage-corrected
      ([leakage_correction](#decisions.leakage_correction)).
    default: size_cut
    options:
      size_cut:
        label: "Size-cut (v1.4.6.3)"
        description: |
          Size cut r_h,gal/r_h,psf > 0.707 on the 2894 deg²
          footprint, including the v1.4.6.3 PSF-size fix.
      initial:
        label: "Initial (v1.4.5)"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Reported beside the fiducial catalog in every version comparison rather than selected: it fails the null tests at the adopted cuts, and the GLASS mock validation and 10,000-bin convergence run exist only for v1.4.6.3."
        description: |
          The looser size cut r_h,gal/r_h,psf > 0.5, the reference
          the size cut is tested against.
      masked:
        label: "Masked (v1.4.8)"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Reported beside the fiducial catalog in every version comparison rather than selected: it fails the null tests at the adopted cuts, and the GLASS mock validation and 10,000-bin convergence run exist only for v1.4.6.3."
        description: |
          Size-cut sample with bright (r < 12) and faint
          (12 < r < 18) stellar-halo masking, leaving 2517 deg².
      relaxed_flags:
        label: "Relaxed flags (v1.4.11.3)"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Reported beside the fiducial catalog in every version comparison rather than selected: it fails the null tests at the adopted cuts, and the GLASS mock validation and 10,000-bin convergence run exist only for v1.4.6.3."
        description: |
          Size-cut sample with relaxed SExtractor deblending flags,
          raising n_eff by 26% on the 2894 deg² footprint.

  fiducial_blind:
    label: "Fiducial blind for reported data vectors"
    tags: [data_selection]
    rationale: |
      Blinding acts on the source n(z): an external coordinator
      produced three variants, two with random shifts. The n(z) does
      not enter the B-mode data vectors, and the covariances barely
      depend on it, since the Gaussian B-mode covariance of a null
      signal is shape noise alone. A single blind therefore [serves
      throughout](#findings.bmode_null_tests_insensitive_to_blinding).
    default: blind_a
    options:
      blind_a:
        label: "Blind A"
      blind_b:
        label: "Blind B"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "The paper reports blind A; B-mode covariances are blind-independent, shown by validation.bb_covariance_blind_independence_evidence."
      blind_c:
        label: "Blind C"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "The paper reports blind A; B-mode covariances are blind-independent, shown by validation.bb_covariance_blind_independence_evidence."

  integration_grid:
    label: "ξ± integration grid for B-mode filters"
    tags: [integration]
    rationale: |
      The pure-mode and COSEBI filters are integrated against ξ±
      measured on a grid much finer than the reporting bins, and the
      grid must be fine enough that the B-mode amplitudes and their
      significance no longer change under refinement. A finer-grid
      run on the fiducial catalog shows they are stable for the
      [pure modes](#analyses.validation.findings.pure_modes_converged_at_1000_bins)
      and the
      [COSEBIs](#analyses.validation.findings.cosebis_verdicts_stable_at_1000_bins),
      where individual high modes move further.
    default: bins_1000
    options:
      bins_1000:
        label: "1000 bins"
        description: |
          1000 logarithmic bins over θ = 0.5'–300', one TreeCorr run
          per catalog variant.
      bins_10000:
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Used only as the convergence check in validation.integration_grid_convergence; the mock measurements and covariance exist on the 1000-bin grid."
        label: "10,000 bins (convergence test)"
        description: |
          Fiducial catalog only.

  pure_eb_integration_method:
    label: "Pure E/B transform quadrature"
    tags: [integration]
    rationale: |
      The Schneider (2022) transform, as implemented in
      `cosmo_numba`, lays a degree-5 local interpolant through the
      integrand samples. The interpolant depends linearly on the
      samples, so the transform is a fixed linear map on ξ_± as long
      as the integration rule does not depend on the data. Adaptive
      quadrature subdivides according to the sampled values, so under
      it the map is weakly non-linear: on noisy input the quadrature
      error correlates with the noise and rectifies into a spurious
      small-θ B mode. The same error is independent noise in every
      realization, so it also inflates every Monte-Carlo-propagated
      covariance. This decision therefore forks the data vectors, the
      mock scatter and the covariance together.

      Integrating the same interpolant with a fixed rule cell by cell
      makes the transform exactly linear, `out = M · [ξ_+ ; ξ_-]`,
      with `M` set by the grid and kernels alone. The fixed operator
      is preferred because it is accurate and, being linear, cannot
      rectify noise.
    default: fixed_operator
    options:
      adaptive_dqags:
        label: "Adaptive dqags"
        description: |
          `cosmo_numba`'s `get_pure_EB_modes` with QUADPACK's `dqags`
          at tolerances epsabs = epsrel = 1e-10, evaluated pointwise
          at the 20 reporting-bin centres. Its data-dependent
          subdivision rectifies noise into a ≈ −0.6 σ mean ξ_+^B
          residual at θ < 3' on the GLASS mocks, and into a −25.7 σ_MC
          small-θ ξ_+^B bias on Monte Carlo noise draws outside this
          analysis's outputs. It is itself inaccurate, up to 15.6%
          wrong on V_- at 1000 integration bins and worsening under
          grid refinement, and it inflates Monte-Carlo-propagated
          covariances: ξ_-^B bin 0 by ×3.3, ξ_-^amb by ×17 at all
          scales, ξ_+^B bin 0 by ×1.13.
      fixed_operator:
        label: "Fixed-quadrature operator M"
        description: |
          The same interpolant and kernels integrated with a
          16-node Gauss-Legendre rule per grid cell, assembled once
          per grid and applied as a matrix product, so noise cannot
          rectify. It agrees with a brute-force integration to
          ≤ 3 × 10⁻¹⁵ of max|ξ|. On the same Monte Carlo noise draws
          its small-θ ξ_+^B bias is −0.9 σ_MC, a residual
          proportional to the injected noise and so finite-draw
          error.

          The operator is evaluated on the fine-grid nodes and its
          output averaged into the reporting bins (weighted per
          [pure_eb_rebinning_weights](#decisions.pure_eb_rebinning_weights)),
          with integration limits from the fine-grid extent: the
          operator evaluates only on grid nodes, the reporting-bin
          centres sit up to 0.32% off them, and the reporting data
          vector is itself a bin average rather than a point
          sample. The two options therefore differ in
          geometry as well as quadrature; the validation shows the
          quadrature term dominates. Rows with fewer than six support
          nodes, too few for the degree-5 interpolant, are rejected;
          none occur on the 1000-bin grid, where the smallest support
          is 29 nodes.

  pure_eb_rebinning_weights:
    label: "Pure-mode rebinning weights"
    tags: [binning]
    rationale: |
      The [averaged geometry](#decisions.pure_eb_integration_method)
      leaves the pure modes on the fine integration nodes, which must
      be averaged into the reporting bins. The pure-mode identity
      holds pointwise in θ, so the local and integral terms must be
      averaged with the *same* weights: on the GLASS mocks every
      hybrid that averages them differently is biased and every
      consistent estimator is unbiased.

      The integral term is smooth and nearly fully correlated across
      the fine nodes of a bin, so any weighting gives it the same
      value, and the two consistent candidates are statistically
      indistinguishable. The weights matter only for the local term,
      the measured ξ_±, and there the pair-count-weighted mean over
      fine bins is by construction the reporting-bin estimator
      ξ-hat_± itself (Asgari et al. 2019, Appendix A). The unweighted
      mean is a different, mildly noisier estimator that is neither
      the measured correlation function nor the bin average of
      theory. Pair-count weighting is adopted. A transform evaluated
      pointwise does no rebinning (`none`).
    default: npairs
    options:
      npairs:
        label: "Pair-count weighted"
        description: |
          Each fine node is weighted by its TreeCorr pair count, so
          the averaged local term is exactly the reporting-bin
          ξ-hat_±.
      uniform:
        label: "Unweighted"
        description: |
          Equal weight per fine node. It differs from pair-count
          weighting by 2.7% on rebinned ξ_+ but is unbiased and
          equally powerful on the mocks (mock scatter 0.98× that of
          pair-count weighting; under the Monte Carlo covariance, data
          ξ_-^B PTE 0.026 against 0.023). Its local term is not the
          measured correlation function.
      none:
        label: "None (pointwise)"
        description: |
          The transform is evaluated directly at the 20 reporting
          bin centres, so no rebinning occurs; the only selection
          consistent with
          [adaptive_dqags](#decisions.pure_eb_integration_method).

  pure_eb_integration_limits:
    label: "Pure-mode integration limits"
    tags: [integration]
    rationale: |
      The Schneider (2022) decomposition is defined on a finite
      [θ_min, θ_max]. A wide interval lets small-θ contamination
      into every reporting bin (ξ_-^B at θ mixes in ξ measured below
      θ); a narrow one discards information and moves the
      estimator. Shrinking the limits inward finds no plateau where
      the estimator settles, so the shrinking measures an operator
      systematic rather than singling out a window.

      The [averaged geometry](#decisions.pure_eb_integration_method)
      keeps the full fine-grid extent. It cannot start at the
      reporting floor: nodes next to θ_min would have fewer support
      nodes than the degree-5 interpolant needs, leaving
      under-determined ξ_- edge rows. Only the pointwise chain, which
      evaluates at the interior bin centres, can use the reporting
      edges. Each geometry therefore has one valid option and any
      other pairing is rejected, so this decision follows the
      integration method.
    default: fine_grid_extent
    options:
      fine_grid_extent:
        label: "Fine-grid extent, 0.5'–300'"
        description: |
          Averaged geometry: fine-grid nodes from the 0.5' grid
          floor to 300'; support below 1' keeps the edge rows
          determined.

          Shrinking these limits inward bin by bin moves the data
          vector non-monotonically, driven entirely by ξ_-^B (ξ_+^B
          stays null at PTE 0.72–0.91), while σ shifts by ≤ 5.6%
          (ξ_+) and ≤ 1.3% (ξ_-). The combined pure-mode p-value
          spans 0.018–0.064 across that scan, an operator systematic
          of about ±0.02 on p. The scan is not an output of this
          analysis and used a separate Monte Carlo covariance, whose
          p-values differ from the reported ones by 0.01–0.02.
      reporting_extent:
        label: "Reporting-grid extent, 1'–250'"
        description: |
          Pointwise only: the reporting limits [1', 250'], which the
          `adaptive_dqags` chain integrates over. Under the averaged
          geometry a 1' floor would leave five ξ_- edge rows with
          fewer than the six support nodes the interpolant needs.

  harmonic_validation_binning:
    label: "Harmonic COSEBI bandpower count"
    tags: [binning]
    rationale: |
      The harmonic COSEBI path sums W_n(ℓ) filters against Cℓ
      bandpowers, so its measurement, covariance and transform must share
      one bin count. Too few bins cannot resolve the filters' oscillations;
      too many make mode-coupling deconvolution unstable.
      The adopted count is the one validated on the GLASS mocks, where
      the low-order modes agree with the configuration-space path. The
      coarser bandpowers of the
      [Cℓ null test](#analyses.catalog_processing.outputs.cl_bandpowers_reporting)
      do not resolve the higher-order oscillations.
    default: bins_96
    options:
      bins_96:
        label: "96 √ℓ-linear bandpowers"
        description: "Validated on the GLASS mocks, where modes n ≤ 6 agree with the configuration-space path."
      bins_128:
        label: "128 √ℓ-linear bandpowers"
        description: "Finer bins than the 96 validated on the mocks."
      bins_32:
        label: "32 √ℓ-linear bandpowers"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Cannot resolve W_n(ℓ) beyond n ≈ 4."

  pte_definition:
    label: "PTE statistical convention"
    tags: [statistics]
    rationale: |
      Every PTE is the χ² tail probability of the measured χ² with
      ν equal to the number of data points in the range, valid for
      linear estimators of Gaussian data. Anderson-Darling or KS
      tests would be harder to interpret as calibrated tails. On the
      GLASS mocks the C_ℓ^BB PTEs are uniform, while the
      configuration-space PTEs
      [skew mildly low](#findings.mock_ptes_skew_low_by_ng_term),
      which calibrating [p_thr](#analyses.significance.decisions.pte_threshold) on the same
      realizations partially absorbs.
    default: chi2_tail
    options:
      chi2_tail:
        label: "χ² tail probability"
        insights: [stebbins96_scalar_perturbations_give_no_bmodes, higher_order_lensing_bmodes_negligible]
      anderson_darling:
        label: "Anderson-Darling"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Paper II computes χ² tails; no Anderson–Darling null statistic or calibration is implemented."
        description: "Not used; harder to interpret as a calibrated tail."
      kolmogorov_smirnov:
        label: "Kolmogorov-Smirnov"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Paper II computes χ² tails; no Kolmogorov–Smirnov null statistic or calibration is implemented."
        description: "Not used."

  leakage_correction:
    label: "PSF-leakage correction"
    tags: [data_selection]
    rationale: |
      Each catalog variant exists with and without Paper I's
      object-wise PSF-leakage correction (binned regression in S/N
      and galaxy-PSF size ratio). Results are reported
      leakage-corrected, as in Papers III and IV, and the correction
      changes no pass/fail conclusion.
    default: applied
    options:
      applied:
        label: "Applied"
        insights: [guerrini25_psf_errors_contaminate_xi]
      uncorrected:
        label: "Uncorrected"
        description: |
          Ellipticities without the leakage correction; used for
          cross-checks only. Against the corrected catalogs,
          individual PTEs shift by at most 0.093 across all catalog
          versions and statistics.

  bandpower_binning:
    label: "Bandpower binning scheme"
    tags: [binning]
    rationale: |
      The Cℓ^BB null tests use Paper IV's data-vector binning, the
      square-root-spaced (ℓ^0.5) scheme Paper IV adopts from DES Y3,
      so the tests probe the bandpowers the inference uses.
      Square-root spacing sits between linear binning, which
      spends most bandpowers at high ℓ, and logarithmic binning,
      which spends most at low ℓ. The
      [harmonic-space COSEBIs](#analyses.validation.outputs.cosebis_harmonic_modes)
      use finer bandpowers in the same scheme, set by
      [harmonic_validation_binning](#decisions.harmonic_validation_binning)
      to resolve the W_n(ℓ) filter oscillations.
    default: bandpowers_32_powspace
    options:
      bandpowers_32_powspace:
        label: "32 √ℓ-spaced over 8 ≤ ℓ ≤ 2048"
      bandpowers_96_powspace:
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Used for the harmonic COSEBI transform, not the BB null test; the mock Cℓ spectra and covariance exist only at 32 bands."
        label: "96 √ℓ-spaced over 8 ≤ ℓ ≤ 2048 (COSEBI transform)"
        description: |
          Fine grid for the harmonic-space COSEBIs; not used by
          the Cℓ^BB null test.
      bandpowers_16_powspace:
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "The mock Cℓ spectra and covariance exist only at 32 bands."
        label: "16 √ℓ-spaced"
        description: |
          Coarser bandpowers, departing from Paper IV's data
          vector.
      bandpowers_64_powspace:
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "The mock Cℓ spectra and covariance exist only at 32 bands."
        label: "64 √ℓ-spaced"
        description: |
          Finer bandpowers, departing from Paper IV's data
          vector.

  noise_bias_correction:
    label: "Shot-noise / noise-bias correction"
    tags: [estimator]
    rationale: |
      Shape noise biases Cℓ auto-spectra by an amount
      that scales with the inverse galaxy density. The paper
      subtracts an analytic shot-noise contribution following
      Paper IV's implementation of the catalog-based estimator,
      which Wolz et al. (2025) show is unbiased against noise
      uncorrelated between sources. A Monte-Carlo estimate is
      the standard alternative for map-based pipelines.
    default: analytic_shot_noise
    options:
      analytic_shot_noise:
        label: "Analytic shot-noise subtraction"
        insights: [wolz25_catalog_based_pseudo_cl]
      mc_noise_bias:
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Not used: the analytic subtraction is unbiased against noise uncorrelated between sources, and no matching mock covariance exists for a Monte Carlo estimate."
        label: "Monte-Carlo noise-bias estimator"
        description: |
          Subtracts the mean Cℓ of ellipticity-randomised
          realizations.

  reporting_binning:
    label: "Reporting-grid angular binning"
    tags: [binning]
    rationale: |
      The reporting grid matches the configuration-space data vector
      of Paper III, so the null tests probe the bins its inference
      uses. Its bin edges also bound the
      [scale cuts](#analyses.significance.decisions.fiducial_scale_cuts), which keep whole
      reporting bins.
    default: bins_20
    options:
      bins_20:
        label: "20 log bins over [1', 250']"
        description: |
          The binning of the paper and of Paper III.
      bins_40:
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "The mock reporting measurements and their matched covariance exist only at 20 bins."
        label: "40 log bins over [1', 250']"
        description: |
          Finer reporting grid for sensitivity studies; not used
          in the paper.

  decomposition_method:
    label: "Pure-mode integral-transform construction"
    tags: [estimator]
    rationale: |
      Schneider et al. (2022) decompose ξ_±(θ) on a finite
      [θ_min, θ_max] into pure E, pure B and ambiguous components
      by integral transforms of the measured ξ_±, with boundary
      functions S_±(θ) and V_±(θ) absorbing the ambiguous-mode
      polynomials a + b θ², c θ⁻² + d θ⁻⁴. Reconstructing the pure
      modes from COSEBI coefficients is mathematically equivalent
      but needs the same angular range for ξ_+ and ξ_-; the direct
      transform lets each carry its own scale cuts, so it is used.
      The transform runs through `cosmo_numba` (Guinot et al. 2026,
      <https://github.com/aguinot/cosmo-numba>), a JIT implementation of
      the Schneider et al. (2022) kernels covering the boundary functions
      S_± and V_± and the integral kernels on the integration grid.
    default: schneider22_integral_transform
    options:
      schneider22_integral_transform:
        label: "Schneider et al. 2022 integral transform"
        insights: [pure_mode_decomposition_unique_on_finite_interval, schneider22_pure_modes_direct_from_xi, guinot26_cosmo_numba_precision]
      cosebi_reconstruction:
        label: "COSEBI-coefficient reconstruction"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Paper II implements the direct Schneider (2022) transform; reconstructing ξ E/B from COSEBI coefficients has no implementation."
        description: |
          Equivalent on a shared [θ_min, θ_max], but does not
          allow independent ξ_+ / ξ_- scale cuts.

  mode_count:
    label: "Number of COSEBI modes computed"
    tags: [estimator]
    rationale: |
      The cosmological E-mode amplitude saturates within the first
      few modes, but systematics need not, so the adopted count is
      conservative for information and matches the mode count used
      to test COSEBI B modes for systematics. The filter roots are
      computed at high precision, so numerics do not set the limit.
      Fewer modes would lose the high-n end of the full-range
      [COSEBI failure signature](#findings.ccd_scale_cosebi_pattern).
      The [convergence test](#analyses.validation.outputs.integration_grid_convergence) covers every
      mode the COSEBI analysis reports, so it takes the same count.
    default: n_max_20
    options:
      n_max_20:
        label: "20 modes"
        insights: [asgari19a_cosebis_nmax20_for_systematics]
        description: |
          Filter roots computed at 120-digit precision.
      n_max_15:
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "The null tests and their mock calibration are defined for n ≤ 6 and n ≤ 20; there is no 15-mode test."
        label: "15 modes"
        description: |
          Drops the high-n modes where the full-range
          repeating-additive signature is most visible.
      n_max_30:
        label: "30 modes"
        description: |
          Not computed.
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: |
          Beyond the n ≤ 20 used for B-mode systematics tests; adds
          noise-dominated degrees of freedom.

  reference_covariance:
    label: "Analytic covariance the mock scatter is compared against"
    tags: [covariance_model]
    rationale: |
      Which analytic covariance the mocks' empirical scatter is held
      against. A signal-free suite's B-mode scatter is its shape noise,
      so the scatter tests a covariance only if the two share a noise
      level. A suite matched to the data's footprint, count and σ_e
      ([mock_suite](#decisions.mock_suite)) shares the data's, and is
      held against the data covariances themselves: the comparison
      then tests the covariance the null tests use. A suite sampled
      differently would, against the data covariance, measure its
      noise mismatch rather than the covariance's accuracy
      ([mocks_are_over_constraining](#analyses.validation.analyses.glass_mocks.findings.mocks_are_over_constraining));
      it is held instead against the covariance *machinery*, the same
      code that builds the fiducial covariance run at the suite's own
      noise. The null tests read the
      [data covariances](#analyses.covariances.outputs.pure_eb_covariance)
      under either selection; the reference covariances are those same
      covariances when the suite matches the data, and otherwise two
      rebuilds of the fiducial primitives at the suite's noise:

      | statistic | reference | traces to |
      |---|---|---|
      | COSEBIs | the ξ_± covariance transformed by `cosebis_covariance_from_xipm_covariance` | the CosmoCov run |
      | ξ_+^B, ξ_-^B, ξ_tot^B | [pure_eb_covariance_reference](#analyses.covariances.outputs.pure_eb_covariance_reference), its propagation through the pure-mode transform | the CosmoCov run |
      | C_ℓ^BB | [cl_cov_reference](#analyses.covariances.outputs.cl_cov_reference), NaMaster iNKA on a catalog's count map and shot noise | itself |

      Five of the six statistics trace to one artifact, the
      [CosmoCov ξ_± run at the reference noise](#analyses.covariances.outputs.cov_integration_reference),
      transformed for COSEBIs and propagated through the Schneider
      (2022) filters for the pure modes. C_ℓ^BB needs no density
      parameter: NaMaster takes the weighted count map and noise bias
      of one realization's catalog summary.

      The CosmoCov rebuild changes only the noise. Shot noise depends
      on the product of galaxy density and area, so the area
      convention cancels there, and both CosmoCov runs use the same
      sky fraction in the cosmic-variance term. A suite on the data's
      footprint with the data's σ_e differs from it in noise by its
      galaxy-count ratio alone, which is what the rebuild follows
      ([clbb_variance_ratios](#analyses.validation.analyses.glass_mocks.outputs.clbb_variance_ratios)).
      The data covariance is preferred whenever the suite allows it,
      since it validates the covariance the significance rests on
      rather than the code that built it.
    default: data_covariance
    options:
      mockmatched:
        label: "Mock-matched"
        description: |
          The fiducial covariance machinery run at the noise of the
          v1.4.6.3_v2 suite: CosmoCov at that suite's n_eff and σ_e, its
          pure-mode propagation, and NaMaster on the count map and shot
          noise of its realization 00001.

          CosmoCov keeps the data's `area = 2894.03` deg² and sets
          `source_n_gal = 5.793 arcmin⁻²` (60.36 M galaxies over that
          area, 0.1% below the 60 423 575 of realization 00001) and
          `sigma_e = 0.37926`. The area is the footprint convention
          shared with Papers III and IV rather than the 2750.65 deg²
          the galaxies occupy, a choice worth about 5% of the
          sample-variance term, inherited from the data covariance.
      data_covariance:
        label: "Data covariance"
        description: |
          The data's own covariances, for the fiducial v1.4.6.3
          leak-corrected catalog at blind A, taken as the reference
          unchanged. Held against a data-matched suite, the mock scatter
          tests them directly; held against a suite sampled differently,
          it measures that suite's noise mismatch.
  mock_suite:
    label: "GLASS realization suite"
    tags: [covariance_model]
    rationale: |
      Which suite of GLASS lognormal realizations the covariances and the
      null-test thresholds are validated on. A suite tests the covariance
      on the sky the null tests use only if it sits on the data's footprint
      with the data's shape noise: the B-mode variance of a signal-free
      field is shape noise, so a suite with more galaxies or a smaller σ_e
      than the catalog has a smaller scatter than the data's covariance
      predicts, and the comparison measures that mismatch rather than the
      covariance. Matching the suite to the fiducial catalog, on its own
      footprint at its weight-effective count and σ_e, lets the mock
      scatter be held against the data's own covariance. A suite sampled
      differently can still validate the covariance *machinery*, run at the
      suite's noise ([reference_covariance](#decisions.reference_covariance)).
    default: data_matched
    options:
      data_matched:
        label: "Data-matched suite"
        insights: [tessore23_glass_lognormal_mocks]
        description: |
          350 realizations at the published generation settings, sampled
          on the fiducial catalog's footprint (its occupied nside-4096
          pixels) at the density and per-component σ_e derived from the
          catalog ([glass_mock_sampling](#analyses.mocks.analyses.generation.outputs.glass_mock_sampling)),
          so each realization's expected count is the catalog's
          weight-effective count. Seeds 1 000 000 + N.
      v1_4_6_3_v2:
        label: "v1.4.6.3_v2 suite"
        insights: [tessore23_glass_lognormal_mocks]
        description: |
          The suite the paper was published with: 350 realizations of
          about 60.4 M unit-weight galaxies at 6.0905 arcmin⁻² and
          σ_e = 0.2684 per component, on the v1.4.6 cut catalog's
          footprint (2757.25 deg²), 17% more than the fiducial catalog's
          51.65 M weight-effective galaxies. Seeds 1 000 000 + N.
      v1_4_6:
        label: "v1.4.6 suite"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: |
          35 078 729 galaxies per realization on a 1600.33 deg² mask
          that is not the data's footprint (the generator's default
          6.0905 arcmin⁻² on a smaller sky).

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Findings: claims derived from this analysis's own measurements. Evidence
# anchors the reported artifacts.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
findings:

  bmodes_null_at_adopted_cuts:
    id: bmodes_null_at_adopted_cuts
    label: "B modes are consistent with zero at the adopted scale cuts"
    claim: |
      UNIONS-3500 weak-lensing B modes are consistent with zero at the
      adopted scale cuts across pure-mode correlation functions,
      COSEBIs, and harmonic-space power spectra. Without scale cuts,
      ξ_+^B and the COSEBIs show significant B modes on small scales,
      whereas ξ_-^B and C_ℓ^BB show a broad, low-level excess with
      little scale dependence; this excess is significant in ξ_-^B on
      large scales and marginal at the fiducial cuts.
    notes: |
      Size-cut catalog at the fiducial cuts: ξ_+^B 0.82, ξ_-^B 0.019,
      ξ_tot^B 0.039, COSEBIs n ≤ 6 0.78, C_ℓ^BB 0.30. The minimum,
      0.019, passes the 0.01 threshold; in the data-matched `baseline`
      suite 45 of 350 systematics-free GLASS realizations (13%; 50/350,
      14%, in `published`) have a lower minimum PTE. On the full range
      ξ_+^B (0.0026), ξ_-^B (0.0019) and COSEBIs n ≤ 6 (1.4×10⁻⁵) fail.
      Treating the two scale-cut boundaries as fitted parameters
      (ν → ν−2) is the most pessimistic degrees-of-freedom treatment;
      it lowers every PTE, and only ξ_-^B falls below 0.01, to 0.005
      ([nu_penalty_verdicts](#outputs.nu_penalty_verdicts)), just below
      the 0.0065 (`0.007` rounded) threshold calibrated at these cuts
      in `baseline` (`0.0039` in `published`).
    created_at: "2026-04-25T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: pte_table_appendix
        quote:
          exact: "Size_cuts,SP_v1.4.6.3_leak_corr,Fiducial,0.777,0.943,0.823,0.0193,0.0387,0.299"
      - id: ev2
        artifact: mock_min_pte_calibration
        quote:
          exact: '"p_global_one_sided_count": 45'
      - id: ev3
        artifact: fig_pure_eb_decomposition
      - id: ev4
        artifact: fig_mock_min_pte
      - id: ev5
        artifact: nu_penalty_verdicts
        quote:
          exact: "Size_cuts,SP_v1.4.6.3_leak_corr,fiducial,xim_B,7,5,16.7177,0.0193098,0.00506742,0.0142423,0,0,0"
    scope: "Size-cut catalog; 12′–83′ in configuration space, 300 < ℓ < 1600 in harmonic space."

  ccd_scale_cosebi_pattern:
    id: ccd_scale_cosebi_pattern
    label: "A CCD-scale COSEBI B-mode pattern, suppressed by the 12′ cut"
    claim: |
      On the full angular range, all catalog versions show an
      oscillatory COSEBI B-mode pattern plausibly caused by a repeating
      additive shear bias at CCD angular scales, as also seen in
      CFHTLenS on the same MegaCam camera. The adopted lower cut
      suppresses this pattern without discarding the angular scales
      that carry most of the cosmological signal.
    notes: |
      The first COSEBI mode of the size-cut catalog reaches 4.1σ on
      the full range and 0.8σ at the fiducial cuts. MegaCam's 40 CCDs
      span 6–14′ individually, and the B-mode contamination
      concentrates at θ_min ≲ 12′
      ([fig_pte_heatmaps](#outputs.fig_pte_heatmaps)). PSF-leakage
      correction does not significantly change the pattern, so its
      origin is either not leakage or leakage beyond the second-order
      model. Whether it arises from the propagation of exposure offsets
      in multi-exposure shape fitting (Paper V) remains open.
    created_at: "2026-04-25T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: fig_cosebis_fiducial
      - id: ev2
        artifact: cosebis_first_mode_significance
        quote:
          exact: '"full_range_significance": 4.08998422120677'
      - id: ev3
        artifact: fig_pte_heatmaps
    scope: "All four ShapePipe v1.4 variants, 1′–250′ and the fiducial cuts."

  filter_functions_set_sensitivity:
    id: filter_functions_set_sensitivity
    label: "Filter functions, not the basis, set null-test sensitivity"
    claim: |
      C_ℓ^BB passes where COSEBIs computed from the same harmonic-space
      bandpowers fail, because the COSEBI filter functions concentrate
      sensitivity on the contaminated scales; COSEBIs from
      configuration and harmonic space agree with each other. A null
      test in one representation therefore cannot validate another,
      and a B-mode failure in any framework warrants scrutiny across
      all of them.
    notes: |
      Size-cut catalog, COSEBIs n ≤ 6: PTE 0.78 (configuration) and
      0.60 (harmonic) at the fiducial cuts, 1.4×10⁻⁵ and 1.6×10⁻⁵ on
      the full range, while C_ℓ^BB passes at 300 < ℓ < 1600 (0.30).
      This supports Asgari et al. (2019) and matches Jefferson et al.
      (2025), who found tomographic bins passing pseudo-C_ℓ tests
      failing under HybridEB.
    created_at: "2026-04-25T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: fig_harmonic_config_cosebis_full
      - id: ev2
        artifact: cosebis_harmonic_config
        quote:
          exact: |
            size_cuts,harmonic,fiducial,0.598,4.58,6
            size_cuts,harmonic,full_range,1.62e-05,32.0,6
            size_cuts,config,fiducial,0.777,,
            size_cuts,config,full_range,1.37e-05,,
    scope: "Size-cut catalog, fiducial and full-range cuts."

  only_size_cut_catalog_passes:
    id: only_size_cut_catalog_passes
    label: "Only the size-cut catalog passes in every representation"
    claim: |
      Of the four catalog variants, only the size-cut catalog passes
      every statistic: tightening the size cut suppresses B-mode power
      in ξ_-^B and harmonic space, adding stellar-halo masks causes a
      failure in ξ_-^B, and COSEBIs (n ≤ 6) pass for all versions.
      Because the same contamination projects differently into
      angular, modal, and multipole representations, demanding that
      all three pass places tighter constraints than any single null
      test.
    notes: |
      Fiducial-cut failures (PTE < 0.01): initial ξ_-^B 0.0012,
      ξ_tot^B 0.0014, C_ℓ^BB 0.0031; masked ξ_-^B 0.0036; relaxed
      flags ξ_-^B 7.5×10⁻⁵, ξ_tot^B 6.7×10⁻⁵, C_ℓ^BB 5.3×10⁻¹⁰. Why
      masking fails ξ_-^B is undetermined: the irregular mask may
      leave more modes ambiguous, or removing noisy regions near bright
      stars may raise the significance of contamination elsewhere. The
      relaxed-flags catalog also raises the total ξ_+ beyond 16′,
      suggesting the admitted objects affect the signal itself.
    created_at: "2026-04-25T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: pte_table_appendix
        quote:
          exact: "Masked,SP_v1.4.8_leak_corr,Fiducial,0.604,0.811,0.864,0.00359,0.0401,0.434"
      - id: ev2
        artifact: pte_table_appendix
        quote:
          exact: "Relaxed_flags,SP_v1.4.11.3_leak_corr,Fiducial,0.824,0.831,0.418,7.48e-05,6.68e-05,5.25e-10"
      - id: ev3
        artifact: pte_table_appendix
        quote:
          exact: "Initial,SP_v1.4.5_leak_corr,Fiducial,0.938,0.611,0.526,0.00119,0.00138,0.00309"
      - id: ev4
        artifact: fig_versions_pure_eb
    scope: "Four ShapePipe v1.4 leakage-corrected variants at the fiducial cuts."

  bmode_null_tests_insensitive_to_blinding:
    id: bmode_null_tests_insensitive_to_blinding
    label: "The B-mode null tests are insensitive to the blinding"
    claim: |
      The n(z) does not enter the B-mode data vectors, and its effect on
      their covariances is negligible: across the three n(z) variants
      they are identical in configuration space, since the Gaussian
      B-mode covariance of a null signal is shape noise alone, and agree
      to better than 0.5% in harmonic space over the fiducial multipole
      range, the residual coming from E-to-B leakage from the mask. A
      single variant is therefore used throughout
      ([fiducial_blind](#decisions.fiducial_blind)).
    created_at: "2026-11-07T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: bb_covariance_blind_independence_evidence
    scope: "Covariances of the three n(z) variants, at the catalog the check selects."

  mock_ptes_skew_low_by_ng_term:
    id: mock_ptes_skew_low_by_ng_term
    label: "Configuration-space PTEs skew mildly low; C_ℓ^BB PTEs are uniform"
    claim: |
      On the clean realizations the C_ℓ^BB PTEs are uniform, while the
      configuration-space PTEs skew mildly low because the analytic σ
      there is slightly smaller than the mock scatter, which raises χ²
      by the inverse square of their ratio. Calibrating the passing
      threshold p_thr on the same realizations partially absorbs this
      skew.
    notes: |
      In the data-matched `baseline` suite (350 realizations held
      directly against the data covariances,
      [mock_campaign_evidence](#outputs.mock_campaign_evidence)),
      ⟨χ²⟩/ν reads: B_{n≤6} 1.070, B_{n≤20} 1.058, ξ_+^B 1.190, ξ_-^B
      1.046, ξ_tot^B 1.124, C_ℓ^BB 0.965 (1.05–1.19 across
      configuration space; 1.10–1.23 in `published`). KS p-values for
      PTE uniformity: B_{n≤6} 3.9×10⁻³, B_{n≤20} 0.021, ξ_+^B
      6.1×10⁻⁷, ξ_-^B 0.19, ξ_tot^B 4.4×10⁻⁶, C_ℓ^BB 0.023 (0.11 in
      `published`).

      The configuration-space excess has the size of the non-Gaussian
      term the Gaussian covariance omits, a comparison of size that the
      paper does not make into an attribution: on the 20-bin reporting
      grid the (G+NG)/G diagonal ratio inside 12′–83′ averages 1.121
      (ξ_+) and 1.123 (ξ_-), a non-Gaussian share of 11% of the
      diagonal variance there and 8% over all bins.

      p_thr is set so a clean sample fails 5% of the time; the paper
      adopts p_thr = 0.01, conservative for nearly all scale-cut
      combinations, against a calibrated 0.0065 (`0.007` rounded) at
      the fiducial cuts in `baseline` (`0.0039` in `published`,
      [mock_min_pte_calibration](#outputs.mock_min_pte_calibration)).
      The observed minimum, ξ_-^B at 0.0193, sits at or above the
      minimum of 45 of 350 clean realizations in `baseline` (12.9%
      one-sided; 70, 20.0%, two-sided; 50/350, 14.3%, in `published`);
      the 5% threshold is 0.0065 one-sided (68% interval 0.0043–0.0095)
      and 0.0038 two-sided.
    created_at: "2026-08-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: mock_campaign_evidence
        quote:
          exact: '"chi2_mean": 8.328292447802596'
      - id: ev2
        artifact: mock_campaign_evidence
        quote:
          exact: '"chi2_mean": 16.396916247026443'
      - id: ev3
        artifact: mock_min_pte_calibration
        quote:
          exact: '"threshold_one_sided": 0.00650753508226542'
      - id: ev4
        artifact: fig_mock_validation
      - id: ev5
        artifact: fig_mock_min_pte
    scope: "Data-matched `baseline` suite against data covariances (and `published` v1.4.6.3_v2 suite against mock-matched covariances), adopted scale cuts, adopted estimators."

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prior insights: quote evidence from the literature. Covers the three
# estimator families' foundational methods papers (Schneider 2022 for pure-mode
# ξ_±, Schneider/Eifler/Krause 2010 for COSEBIs, Wolz/Alonso/Nicola 2025 for
# catalog-based pseudo-Cℓ, with Becker/Rozo 2016 as a related estimator),
# Hartlap 2007 for the sample-covariance bias correction, Asgari 2019a for
# the repeating-additive B-mode signature, and Planck 2020 for the fiducial
# cosmology. The 1000-bin integration-grid choice is supported by
# its own 10,000-bin convergence check and does not carry a prior
# insight.
#
# A second group covers the accuracy of the analytic pseudo-Cℓ Gaussian
# covariance that the harmonic-space B-mode null test relies on: Efstathiou
# 2004 for the narrow-kernel assumption itself, García-García 2019 for the
# NKA's failure on B-mode spectra and at ℓ ≲ 50, Nicola 2021 for the improved
# NKA (the estimator actually used) and its residual low-ℓ and E/B-mixing
# errors, Alonso 2019 for why an unpurified Cℓ^BB variance is dominated by
# leaked E modes, and Wolz 2026 for the catalog-based iNKA's ℓ ≳ 10
# B-mode validity floor. Together these motivate validating the covariance on
# the GLASS mocks; none of them predicts the size of the effect for a footprint
# as small and fragmented as UNIONS.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
prior_insights:
  asgari19a_cosebis_nmax20_for_systematics:
    id: asgari19a_cosebis_nmax20_for_systematics
    label: "Twenty COSEBI modes cover cosmology and systematics (Asgari et al. 2019)"
    claim: |
      COSEBI E-mode predictions vanish beyond the first ~7 modes, so
      high modes carry no cosmological information, but systematic
      signals need not follow that behaviour and can be significant
      at large n. Truncating at n = 20 covers both the cosmological
      and the systematic-diagnostic range.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/201834379"
        quote:
          exact: "Therefore, we do not expect to gain any cosmological information from these modes."
        location:
          page: 7
      - id: ev2
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/201834379"
        quote:
          exact: "On the other hand the signal from systematic effects does not necessarily follow the same behaviour."
        location:
          page: 7
      - id: ev3
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/201834379"
        quote:
          exact: "which encompasses modes that are important for both cosmological and systematic analyses."
        location:
          page: 7
    scope: |
      COSEBI B-mode analysis of KiDS-450, DES-SV and CFHTLenS
      (Asgari et al. 2019a, §4); same n_max = 20 as Paper II.

  schneider22_pure_modes_direct_from_xi:
    id: schneider22_pure_modes_direct_from_xi
    label: "Pure modes come straight from ξ± (Schneider et al. 2022)"
    claim: |
      Pure-mode correlation functions and COSEBIs carry the same
      information, but the pure modes can be computed directly from
      ξ_± without the (infinite) COSEBI set; in practice the
      equivalence is only approximate, because of the finite number
      of COSEBI modes and the finite ξ_± binning.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/202142479"
        quote:
          exact: "However, as we show here, they can also be obtained without first calculating the (infinite) set of COSEBIs."
        location:
          page: 6
      - id: ev2
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/202142479"
        quote:
          exact: "In practice, this exact equivalence will apply only approximately, due to the finite number of COSEBI modes and the finite binning of the correlation functions"
        location:
          page: 6
    scope: "Schneider et al. 2022, A&A 664, A77 — §3.3–3.4."

  guinot26_cosmo_numba_precision:
    id: guinot26_cosmo_numba_precision
    label: "cosmo-numba computes COSEBIs and pure modes at the needed precision (Guinot et al. 2026)"
    claim: |
      `cosmo-numba` computes COSEBIs, whose weight functions need
      ~80-digit precision (float64 is not sufficient; at that
      precision it reproduces the original implementation exactly),
      and the Schneider et al. 2022 pure-mode correlation functions,
      which are less numerically demanding but need a fast implementation.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.2603.18419"
        quote:
          exact: "We can see that classic float64 precision would not be sufficient, and with a precision of 80 our code exactly recovers the results from the original implementation."
        location:
          page: 3
      - id: ev2
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.2603.18419"
        quote:
          exact: "Those integrals are less numerically challenging than the COSEBIs, but having a fast computation is necessary for their integration in an inference pipeline."
        location:
          page: 2
    scope: "Guinot et al. 2026, arXiv 2603.18419 — software paper by a Paper II co-author."

  hartlap07_correction:
    id: hartlap07_correction
    label: "Inverted sample covariances need the Hartlap factor (Hartlap et al. 2007)"
    claim: |
      The inverse of a covariance estimated from N independent
      Gaussian samples of a length-p data vector is biased; the
      factor (N - p - 2) / (N - 1) removes the bias. An
      analytic covariance has no sampling noise and needs no
      correction.
    created_at: "2026-04-25T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361:20066170"
        quote:
          exact: |
            We find that the inverse of the maximum-likelihood
            estimator of the covariance is biased, the amount of
            bias depending on the ratio of the number of bins
            (data vector variables), p, to the number of data
            sets, n. This bias inevitably leads to an -- in
            extreme cases catastrophic -- underestimation of
            the size of the confidence regions.
          prefix: "Methods. We perform Monte-Carlo simulations to investigate the behaviour of estimators for the inverse covariance matrix"
          suffix: "We report on a method to remove this bias for the idealised case of Gaussian errors and statistically independent data vectors."
        location:
          page: 1
    scope: "Sample covariances of Gaussian data (Hartlap et al. 2007, Eq. 17)"

  pure_mode_decomposition_unique_on_finite_interval:
    id: pure_mode_decomposition_unique_on_finite_interval
    label: "ξ± on a finite interval split uniquely into pure modes"
    claim: |
      Measured ξ_±(θ) on a finite interval [θ_min, θ_max]
      decompose uniquely into pure-mode functions, ξ_+ = ξ_+^E +
      ξ_+^B + ξ_+^amb and ξ_- = ξ_-^E − ξ_-^B + ξ_-^amb. This is the
      basis of the configuration-space pure-mode null test.
    created_at: "2026-04-25T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/202142479"
        quote:
          exact: |
            we derive explicit equations for the pure-mode
            shear correlation functions, ξ_±^E/B(θ), and their
            ambiguous components, ξ_±^amb(θ), that can be

          prefix: "ambiguous modes that cannot uniquely be assigned to either E- or B-mode shear. In this paper"

        location:

  repeating_additive_bias_signature:

    label: "A CCD-scale additive pattern leaves oscillating COSEBI B modes"

  wolz25_catalog_based_pseudo_cl:

    claim: |

  stebbins96_scalar_perturbations_give_no_bmodes:
    id: stebbins96_scalar_perturbations_give_no_bmodes
    label: "Density perturbations make no B modes (Stebbins 1996)"
    claim: |
      In the weak-lensing limit, scalar (density) perturbations
      produce only scalar (E-mode) shear; vector and tensor
      perturbations could source pseudo-scalar (B-mode) shear but
      are expected to be very small, so no significant B-mode shear
      is expected from lensing. This is the premise of testing the
      measured B modes against zero.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.astro-ph/9609149"
        quote:
          exact: "Nevertheless it is true that 3-d scalar perturbations will only produce 2-d scalar shear, at least in the weak lensing limit."
        location:
          page: 3
      - id: ev2
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.astro-ph/9609149"
        quote:
          exact: "Thus we really do not expect there to be any significant pseudo-scalar shear."
        location:
          page: 3
    scope: "Weak-lensing limit (Stebbins 1996, astro-ph/9609149, §2)"

  higher_order_lensing_bmodes_negligible:
    id: higher_order_lensing_bmodes_negligible
    label: "Higher-order lensing B modes are negligible"
    claim: |
      Lensing B modes beyond first order (Born corrections,
      lens–lens coupling, source-redshift clustering) are at least
      two orders of magnitude below the E-mode power, and the
      clustering term is very small above a few arcminutes. At the
      scales tested here a detected B mode points to systematics, so
      the null model C^BB = 0 needs no theory template.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.astro-ph/0202411"
        quote:
          exact: "We show all these corrections are at least two orders of magnitude below the convergence or E-mode power and hence relevant only to future ultra high precision measurements."
        location:
          page: 1
      - id: ev2
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.astro-ph/0202411"
        quote:
          exact: "validate the use of current large scale structure weak lensing predictions for cosmological studies and future use of B-modes as a monitor of systematic effects."
        location:
          page: 1
      - id: ev3
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.astro-ph/0112441"
        quote:
          exact: "the resulting B-mode is very small on angular scales larger than a few arcminutes, but its relative contribution rises quickly towards smaller angular scales"
        location:
          page: 1
    scope: "Lensing-induced B modes (Cooray & Hu 2002; Schneider, van Waerbeke & Mellier 2002)"
    notes: |
      Intrinsic alignments (Crittenden et al. 2002) are a further
      B-mode source not bounded by these papers.

  guerrini25_psf_errors_contaminate_xi:
    id: guerrini25_psf_errors_contaminate_xi
    label: "PSF errors leak into ξ± on UNIONS (Guerrini et al. 2025)"
    claim: |
      PSF-model errors add systematics to the shear two-point
      correlation function; galaxy–PSF (τ) and PSF–PSF (ρ)
      correlations with a semi-analytic covariance quantify that
      leakage on UNIONS data, and frame the assessment of the
      catalogs' PSF-leakage correction.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/202453512"
        quote:
          exact: "The latter can be a source of systematics that affect the shear two-point correlation function."
          prefix: "precise measurements of galaxy shapes and therefore an accurate knowledge of the PSF model."
        location:
          page: 1
      - id: ev2
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/202453512"
        quote:
          exact: "They provide fast and accurate diagnostics on PSF systematics that are crucial to understand in the context of cosmic shear studies."
        location:
          page: 1
    scope: "PSF systematics in UNIONS (Guerrini et al. 2025, A&A)"
    notes: |
      The correction itself is Paper I's; Guerrini et al. supply the

  tessore23_glass_lognormal_mocks:
    id: tessore23_glass_lognormal_mocks
    label: "GLASS lognormal light cones reproduce two-point statistics (Tessore et al. 2023)"
    claim: |
      GLASS builds a light cone of matter and weak-lensing fields as
      nested shells, transforming Gaussian random fields (including
      lognormal) to essentially arbitrary precision, and reproduces
      the two-point statistics of clustering and weak lensing at the
      per-cent level. Its realizations are therefore an adequate
      systematics-free reference for B-mode estimator and covariance
      validation, but carry only lognormal non-Gaussianity.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.2302.01942"
        quote:
          exact: "also introduces a new technique to generate transformations of Gaussian random fields (including lognormal) to essentially arbitrary precision"
        location:
          page: 1
      - id: ev2
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.2302.01942"
        quote:
          exact: "readily produces simulated data sets with per cent-level accurate two-point statistics of galaxy clustering and weak lensing"
        location:
          page: 1
    scope: "Tessore et al. 2023, OJAp 6, 11 (abstract); the UNIONS suite itself is Paper III's."

analyses:

  significance:
    path: ./analyses/significance

  validation:
    path: ./analyses/validation

    path: ./analyses/catalog_processing

  mocks:
    path: ./analyses/mocks
texts.universes/baseline.yaml:
id: baseline
description: |
  The accepted paper's selection on mocks matched to the data: the
  data-matched GLASS suite, sampled on the fiducial catalog's footprint at
  its weight-effective count and shape dispersion, with the mock scatter
  held against the data's own covariances. It differs from `published` in
  the mock suite and the reference covariance alone.

decisions:
  fiducial_catalog: size_cut
  leakage_correction: applied
  fiducial_blind: blind_a
  integration_grid: bins_1000
  # The operator and its geometry are described on the root decision's option.
  pure_eb_integration_method: fixed_operator
  # Pair-count weighting: the averaged local term is the reporting-bin ξ.
  pure_eb_rebinning_weights: npairs
  # Wide [grid floor, 300'] window: retain support below the 1' reporting floor.
  pure_eb_integration_limits: fine_grid_extent
  harmonic_validation_binning: bins_96
  pte_definition: chi2_tail
  bandpower_binning: bandpowers_32_powspace
  noise_bias_correction: analytic_shot_noise
  reporting_binning: bins_20
  decomposition_method: schneider22_integral_transform
  mode_count: n_max_20
  reference_covariance: data_covariance
  mock_suite: data_matched

analyses:
  covariances:
    universe: baseline
  catalog_processing:
    universe: baseline
  mocks:
    universe: baseline
  validation:
    universe: baseline
  significance:
    universe: baseline
texts.universes/preprint_v2.yaml:
id: preprint_v2
description: |
  The selection of the paper before the referee report, arXiv
  2604.03227v2: adaptive-quadrature pointwise pure
  E/B modes with a Monte Carlo covariance and the nominal 0.05 PTE
  threshold. The accepted paper is `published`. Both universes validate
  on the published v1.4.6.3_v2 GLASS suite against covariances rebuilt
  at its noise, so the mock-based outputs here are the submitted choices
  on that suite rather than the submitted paper's v1.4.6 mocks.

  Its pure-mode fiducial window is the declared 12'–83' (seven reporting
  bins). The submitted paper's printed fiducial pure-mode PTEs read an
  eighth bin, 9.1'–83' (ξ_tot^B 0.18 there, 0.16 here); its full-range
  PTEs are the same.

decisions:
  fiducial_catalog: size_cut
  leakage_correction: applied
  fiducial_blind: blind_a
  integration_grid: bins_1000
  # cosmo_numba's get_pure_EB_modes, integrated with QUADPACK dqags.
  pure_eb_integration_method: adaptive_dqags
  # The pointwise chain evaluates the transform at the 20 reporting bin centres,
  # so nothing is rebinned; the only selection consistent with adaptive_dqags.
  pure_eb_rebinning_weights: none
  # The transform limits [1', 250'].
  pure_eb_integration_limits: reporting_extent
  harmonic_validation_binning: bins_96
  pte_definition: chi2_tail
  bandpower_binning: bandpowers_32_powspace
  noise_bias_correction: analytic_shot_noise
  reporting_binning: bins_20
  decomposition_method: schneider22_integral_transform
  mode_count: n_max_20
  reference_covariance: mockmatched
  mock_suite: v1_4_6_3_v2

analyses:
  covariances:
    universe: preprint_v2
  catalog_processing:
    universe: preprint_v2
  mocks:
    universe: preprint_v2
  validation:
    universe: preprint_v2
  significance:
    universe: preprint_v2
texts.universes/published.yaml:
id: published
description: |
  The selection the accepted paper (A&A, 2026) was computed with:
  the exactly linear fixed-quadrature Schneider-2022 operator in the
  single-grid transform-averaged geometry (fine-grid evaluation,
  `[θ_min, θ_max]` at the fine-grid extent), with the
  pair-count-weighted mean from the 1000 fine nodes into the 20
  reporting bins, the exact linear covariance, and the mock-calibrated
  threshold on the minimum PTE. Its mock validation runs on the published
  v1.4.6.3_v2 GLASS suite, 17% denser than the data, against covariances
  rebuilt at that suite's noise. The selection it revises is the
  `preprint_v2` universe, which differs in quadrature, geometry,
  covariance and threshold together.

decisions:
  fiducial_catalog: size_cut
  leakage_correction: applied
  fiducial_blind: blind_a
  integration_grid: bins_1000
  # The operator and its geometry are described on the root decision's option.
  pure_eb_integration_method: fixed_operator
  # Pair-count weighting: the averaged local term is the reporting-bin ξ.
  pure_eb_rebinning_weights: npairs
  # Wide [grid floor, 300'] window: retain support below the 1' reporting floor.
  pure_eb_integration_limits: fine_grid_extent
  harmonic_validation_binning: bins_96
  pte_definition: chi2_tail
  bandpower_binning: bandpowers_32_powspace
  noise_bias_correction: analytic_shot_noise
  reporting_binning: bins_20
  decomposition_method: schneider22_integral_transform
  mode_count: n_max_20
  reference_covariance: mockmatched
  mock_suite: v1_4_6_3_v2

analyses:
  covariances:
    universe: published
  catalog_processing:
    universe: published
  mocks:
    universe: published
  validation:
    universe: published
  significance:
    universe: published
texts.analyses/significance/astra.yaml:
version: "0.0.14"
name: "B-mode significance"
description: |
  Where data meet covariance: each B-mode statistic in units of its
  uncertainty. The data vectors with their error bars, χ² PTE matrices over
  every scale-cut pair for each statistic and catalog version, the mock
  calibration of the minimum PTE, the PTE tables and heatmaps, the primary null
  test and the numbers the paper quotes.

inputs:
  - id: survey_areas
    from: ../survey_areas

  - id: xi_integration

  - id: xi_sweep
    from: ../catalog_processing.xi_sweep

  - id: cl_sweep

  - id: cosebis_modes_sweep

  - id: pure_eb_covariance

  - id: pure_eb_covariance_sweep
    from: ../covariances.pure_eb_covariance_sweep

  - id: cosebis_covariance

  - id: cosebis_covariance_sweep
    from: ../covariances.cosebis_covariance_sweep

  - id: cov_integration
    from: ../covariances.cov_integration

  - id: cov_sweep
    from: ../covariances.cov_sweep

  - id: cov_reporting_g
    from: ../covariances.cov_reporting_g

  - id: cov_reporting_ng
    from: ../covariances.cov_reporting_ng

  - id: cl_cov_reporting
    from: ../covariances.cl_cov_reporting

  - id: cl_cov_sweep
    from: ../covariances.cl_cov_sweep

  - id: mock_per_mock_statistics
    from: ../validation.mock_per_mock_statistics

  - id: mock_campaign_evidence
