  - id: cosebis_harmonic_metrics_full
    from: ../validation.cosebis_harmonic_metrics_full

  - id: cosebis_harmonic_version_ptes
    from: ../validation.cosebis_harmonic_version_ptes

outputs:
  - id: pure_eb_data_vector_figure
    type: figure
    description: |
      Pure E/B decomposition (Schneider et al. 2022) of the measured
      ξ_+ (left) and ξ_- (right) for the [fiducial
      catalog](#decisions.fiducial_catalog), plotted as θξ × 10⁴:
      total (black circles), E mode (blue squares), B mode (crimson
      crosses) and ambiguous (grey triangles). B modes should vanish
      for pure lensing and so diagnose systematics; ambiguous modes
      capture boundary effects from the finite angular range. Error
      bars on the total come from the
      [reporting-grid CosmoCov covariance](#inputs.cov_reporting_ng),
      those on the modes from the [pure-mode covariance](#inputs.pure_eb_covariance). Grey shading
      marks scales outside the fiducial cuts.
    format: png
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, pte_definition, leakage_correction, fiducial_blind, reporting_binning]
    inputs: [pure_eb_data, pure_eb_covariance, cov_reporting_ng]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/pure_eb_data_vector.py
        --fiducial-catalog {decisions.fiducial_catalog} --leakage-correction {decisions.leakage_correction} --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind} --reporting-binning {decisions.reporting_binning}
        --pure-eb-data {inputs.pure_eb_data}
        --pure-eb-covariance {inputs.pure_eb_covariance}
        --reporting-cov {inputs.cov_reporting_ng}
        --out-file {output}

  - id: cosebis_data_vector_figure
    type: figure
    format: png
    description: |
      COSEBI B-mode amplitudes for the [fiducial
      catalog](#decisions.fiducial_catalog), normalized by
      uncertainty (B_n/σ_n), at the fiducial scale cuts of 12–83 arcmin
      (filled circles) and over the full angular range of 1–250 arcmin
      (open diamonds). Modes n > 6 are shaded; the n ≤ 6 subset captures
      nearly all cosmological information.
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind]
    inputs: [cosebis_modes_data, cosebis_covariance]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/cosebis_data_vector.py
        --plot-from-modes {inputs.cosebis_modes_data}
        --covariance {inputs.cosebis_covariance}
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "4GB" }

  - id: cl_data_vector_figure
    type: figure
    description: |
      C_ℓ^BB/σ (top) and C_ℓ^EB/σ (bottom) for the [fiducial
      catalog](#decisions.fiducial_catalog). C_ℓ^BB is
      predominantly positive across the fiducial range; C_ℓ^EB
      scatters symmetrically around zero, suggesting that any
      B-mode contamination is not strongly correlated with the
      lensing signal.
    format: png
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, pte_definition, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [cl_bandpowers_reporting, cl_cov_reporting]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/cl_data_vector.py
        --fiducial-catalog {decisions.fiducial_catalog} --leakage-correction {decisions.leakage_correction}
        --fiducial-version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})"
        --fiducial-cl-path {inputs.cl_bandpowers_reporting}
        --fiducial-cl-cov-path {inputs.cl_cov_reporting}
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 2, memory: "8GB" }

  - id: pure_eb_version_comparison_figure
    type: figure
    description: |
      Pure-mode data vectors across catalog versions: initial (red
      circles), size-cut/fiducial (olive squares), masked (teal
      diamonds) and relaxed-flags (purple triangles). Upper panels show
      the total θξ_+ and θξ_-, with the pure E-mode σ as error bars;
      lower panels the B modes ξ_±^B/σ. Rectangles span the range
      across versions in each bin, horizontal lines mark the fiducial
      value, and grey shading marks scales outside the fiducial cuts.
      Only the size-cut catalog passes all statistics at the fiducial
      scale cuts ([PTE table](#outputs.pte_table_appendix)).
    format: png
    decisions: [pte_definition, fiducial_catalog, leakage_correction, fiducial_blind, reporting_binning]
    inputs: [pure_eb_data, pure_eb_sweep, pure_eb_covariance, pure_eb_covariance_sweep]
    recipe:
      command: >
        d=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.pure_eb_sweep} -C $d &&
        c=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.pure_eb_covariance_sweep} -C $c &&
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/pure_eb_version_comparison.py
        --fiducial-catalog {decisions.fiducial_catalog} --leakage-correction {decisions.leakage_correction} --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind} --reporting-binning {decisions.reporting_binning}
        --results-dir $d
        --cov-dir $c
        --fiducial-version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})"
        --fiducial-pure-eb-data {inputs.pure_eb_data}
        --fiducial-pure-eb-covariance {inputs.pure_eb_covariance}
        --out-file {output}

  - id: cosebis_version_comparison_figure
    type: figure
    format: png
    description: |
      COSEBI B-mode amplitudes B_n/σ_n across catalog versions at full
      range (upper) and fiducial cuts (lower), per version:
      initial (red circles), size-cut/fiducial (olive squares), masked
      (teal diamonds), and relaxed-flags (purple triangles). Rectangles
      delineate each mode in the horizontal direction and span the range
      of values across versions in the vertical direction; horizontal
      lines mark the fiducial value. A light band covers n ≤ 6. Only the
      size-cut catalog passes all statistics at the fiducial scale cuts
      ([PTE table](#outputs.pte_table_appendix)).
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, mode_count, leakage_correction, reporting_binning]
    inputs: [cosebis_modes_data, cosebis_modes_sweep, cosebis_covariance, cosebis_covariance_sweep]
    recipe:
      command: >
        m=$(mktemp -d) && c=$(mktemp -d) &&
        tar xzf {inputs.cosebis_modes_sweep} -C $m &&
        tar xzf {inputs.cosebis_covariance_sweep} -C $c &&
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/cosebis_version_comparison.py
        --fiducial-catalog {decisions.fiducial_catalog} --leakage-correction {decisions.leakage_correction} --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind} --reporting-binning {decisions.reporting_binning} --mode-count {decisions.mode_count}
        --results-dir $m
        --cov-dir $c
        --fiducial-version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})"
        --fiducial-modes-path {inputs.cosebis_modes_data}
        --fiducial-covariance-path {inputs.cosebis_covariance}
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 2, memory: "8GB" }

  - id: cl_version_comparison_figure
    type: figure
    description: |
      C_ℓ^BB/σ and C_ℓ^EB/σ across catalog versions: initial (red
      circles), size-cut/fiducial (olive squares), masked (teal
      diamonds) and relaxed-flags (purple triangles). Rectangles
      span each bin horizontally and the range across versions
      vertically; horizontal lines mark the fiducial value; shaded
      bands mark multipoles outside the fiducial cuts. Only the
      size-cut catalog passes all statistics at the fiducial scale cuts
      ([PTE table](#outputs.pte_table_appendix)).
    format: png
    inputs: [cl_sweep, cl_cov_sweep, cl_bandpowers_reporting, cl_cov_reporting]
    decisions: [pte_definition, fiducial_catalog, leakage_correction]
    recipe:
      command: >
        d=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.cl_sweep} -C $d &&
        k=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.cl_cov_sweep} -C $k &&
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/cl_version_comparison.py
        --fiducial-catalog {decisions.fiducial_catalog} --leakage-correction {decisions.leakage_correction}
        --results-dir $d
        --cov-dir $k
        --fiducial-version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})"
        --fiducial-cl-path {inputs.cl_bandpowers_reporting}
        --fiducial-cl-cov-path {inputs.cl_cov_reporting}
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 2, memory: "8GB" }

  - id: cosebis_first_mode_significance
    type: data
    format: json
    description: |
      First-mode COSEBI B-mode significance B_1/σ_1 for the
      fiducial catalog, from
      [cosebis_modes_data](#inputs.cosebis_modes_data) and
      [cosebis_covariance](#inputs.cosebis_covariance). The
      `value` is the full-range (1–250 arcmin) significance, the
      >4σ first-mode excess visible in
      [fig_cosebis_fiducial](#../outputs.fig_cosebis_fiducial); the
      JSON also carries the fiducial-cut significance, below 1σ.
    inputs: [cosebis_modes_data, cosebis_covariance]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/emit_cosebis_first_mode_significance.py
        --cosebis-modes-npz {inputs.cosebis_modes_data}
        --cosebis-covariance-npz {inputs.cosebis_covariance}
        --out-file {output}

  - id: pure_eb_pte_per_cut
    type: data
    description: |
      ξ_+^B, ξ_-^B and joint ξ_tot^B χ² PTE matrices for the
      fiducial catalog (blind A) over every (θ_min, θ_max) index pair
      of the 20-bin `geomspace(1', 250', 21)` grid; the COSEBI
      [scale-cut pair grid](#decisions.scale_cut_pair_grid) is a subset of it.
      The χ² applies the [Hartlap finite-sample
      correction](#../analyses.covariances.decisions.pure_eb_covariance_method) when the
      covariance is a Monte Carlo estimate and none when it is exact.
    format: npz
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, pte_definition, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [pure_eb_data, pure_eb_covariance]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/calculate_pure_eb_ptes.py
        --version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})" --blind "$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py fiducial_blind {decisions.fiducial_blind})"
        --pure-eb-data {inputs.pure_eb_data}
        --pure-eb-covariance {inputs.pure_eb_covariance}
        --npatch 1
        --out-file {output}

  - id: cosebis_pte_per_cut
    # Fiducial-catalog COSEBI PTE matrices at blind A over all stable scale-cut
    # pairs of `geomspace(1', 250', 21)`, for n <= 6 and n <= 20. Read by the
    # configuration-space PTE products and the mock minimum-PTE calibration.
    from: cosebis_pte_grid.cosebis_pte_matrix

  - id: cl_pte_per_cut
    type: data
    description: |
      Cℓ^BB null-test PTEs for all eight catalog variants (four
      catalogs, with and without leakage correction) over a grid of
      (ℓ_min, ℓ_max) bandpower ranges, using the
      [iNKA Gaussian bandpower covariances](#../analyses.covariances.outputs.cl_cov_sweep). The
      [adopted 300 < ℓ < 1600
      cut](#decisions.fiducial_scale_cuts) is one cell of the
      grid, which the
      [harmonic-space PTE heatmap](#outputs.cl_pte_heatmap_figure)
      shows.
    format: npz
    inputs: [cl_sweep, cl_cov_sweep, cl_bandpowers_reporting, cl_cov_reporting]
    decisions: [pte_definition, fiducial_catalog, leakage_correction, fiducial_blind]
    recipe:
      command: >
        d=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.cl_sweep} -C $d &&
        k=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.cl_cov_sweep} -C $k &&
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/harmonic_space_pte_matrices.py
        --fiducial-catalog {decisions.fiducial_catalog} --leakage-correction {decisions.leakage_correction} --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind}
        --results-dir $d
        --cov-dir $k
        --fiducial-version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})"
        --fiducial-cl-path {inputs.cl_bandpowers_reporting}
        --fiducial-cl-cov-path {inputs.cl_cov_reporting}
        --emit matrices
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 2, memory: "8GB" }

  - id: pure_eb_ptes
    type: data
    description: |
      Pure-mode PTE matrices (ξ_+^B, ξ_-^B, joint ξ_tot^B over the
      (θ_min, θ_max) scale-cut grid) for the seven catalog versions of
      [pure_eb_sweep](#inputs.pure_eb_sweep), one
      `{ver}_A_pure_eb_ptes.npz` each, computed as
      [pure_eb_pte_per_cut](#outputs.pure_eb_pte_per_cut) is, with the
      [covariance-dependent Hartlap
      treatment](#../analyses.covariances.decisions.pure_eb_covariance_method), from that
      version's data vector and pure-mode covariance. Feeds the
      per-version [PTE
      heatmaps](#outputs.pte_heatmaps_figure).
    format: tar.gz
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, pte_definition, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [pure_eb_sweep, pure_eb_covariance_sweep]
    recipe:
      command: |
        set -e
        d=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.pure_eb_sweep} -C $d
        c=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.pure_eb_covariance_sweep} -C $c
        o=$(mktemp -d)
        b="$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py fiducial_blind {decisions.fiducial_blind})"
        versions=$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction} --nonfiducial)
        for ver in $versions; do
          python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/calculate_pure_eb_ptes.py \
            --version "$ver" --blind "$b" \
            --pure-eb-data "$d/$ver"_pure_eb_data.npz \
            --pure-eb-covariance "$c/$ver"_"$b"_pure_eb_covariance.npz \
            --npatch 1 --out "$o"
        done
        tar czf {output} -C $o .
      resources: { cpus: 4, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: cosebis_ptes
    # The COSEBI PTE matrices of the seven other catalog versions.
    from: cosebis_pte_scan.cosebis_ptes_bundle

  - id: config_space_pte_data
    type: data
    format: json
    description: |
      ξ_+^B, ξ_-^B, joint ξ_tot^B and COSEBI B_n (n ≤ 6 and n ≤ 20) χ²
      PTE matrices over the (θ_min, θ_max) pair grid of
      `geomspace(1', 250', 21)`, for all four catalog versions with and
      without leakage correction, with the values at the
      [adopted 12'–83' cut](#decisions.fiducial_scale_cuts) and over
      the full range. The adopted-cut values are read from the grid
      cell of reporting bins 9–15, the bins the cut keeps.
      All three statistics share the reporting bins, so a cut is the
      same window in every panel; COSEBIs need at least two bins, so
      their panels leave the single-bin cuts empty. Feeds the
      config-space columns of the per-version PTE table and the
      configuration-space PTE heatmaps.
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, leakage_correction, reporting_binning, fiducial_blind]
    inputs:
      - pure_eb_ptes
      - cosebis_ptes
      - pure_eb_pte_per_cut
      - cosebis_pte_per_cut
    recipe:
      command: >
        d_pe=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.pure_eb_ptes} -C $d_pe &&
        d_cb=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.cosebis_ptes} -C $d_cb &&
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/config_space_pte_matrices.py
        --fiducial-catalog {decisions.fiducial_catalog} --leakage-correction {decisions.leakage_correction} --reporting-binning {decisions.reporting_binning}
        --pte-intermediate-dir $d_pe
        --cosebis-pte-dir $d_cb
        --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind}
        --fiducial-version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})"
        --fiducial-pure-eb-pte-path {inputs.pure_eb_pte_per_cut}
        --fiducial-cosebis-pte-path {inputs.cosebis_pte_per_cut}
        --emit evidence
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 4, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: harmonic_space_pte_data
    type: data
    format: json
    description: |
      Cℓ^BB χ² PTE matrices over the (ℓ_min, ℓ_max) pair grid of the
      32 bandpowers spanning 8 ≤ ℓ ≤ 2048, for all four catalog
      versions with and without leakage correction, with the values at
      the [adopted 300 < ℓ < 1600 cut](#decisions.fiducial_scale_cuts)
      and over the full range.
      Feeds the harmonic column of the per-version PTE table and
      the Cℓ^BB PTE heatmap.
    inputs:
      - cl_sweep
      - cl_cov_sweep
      - cl_bandpowers_reporting
      - cl_cov_reporting
    decisions: [pte_definition, fiducial_catalog, leakage_correction, fiducial_blind]
    recipe:
      command: >
        d_cl=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.cl_sweep} -C $d_cl &&
        d_cov=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.cl_cov_sweep} -C $d_cov &&
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/harmonic_space_pte_matrices.py
        --fiducial-catalog {decisions.fiducial_catalog} --leakage-correction {decisions.leakage_correction} --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind}
        --results-dir $d_cl
        --cov-dir $d_cov
        --fiducial-version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})"
        --fiducial-cl-path {inputs.cl_bandpowers_reporting}
        --fiducial-cl-cov-path {inputs.cl_cov_reporting}
        --emit evidence
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 4, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: mock_min_pte_calibration
    type: data
    format: json
    description: |
      Calibration of the min-PTE criterion on the clean realizations,
      at the fiducial cuts (top level) and over the full range
      (`full_range`): the data's minimum PTE across the six
      statistics, the fraction of clean mocks at or below it (one- and
      two-sided), and the min-PTE threshold for a 5% global
      false-alarm rate, each with a 68% interval (Wilson for
      fractions, bootstrap for thresholds). The fiducial observed PTEs
      are taken from the pure-mode and COSEBI matrices at bins 9–15
      (edge indices 9/16) and C_ℓ^BB at 300 < ℓ < 1600; `full_range`
      uses the [0, 19] matrix cells and all 32 C_ℓ bands (1–250 arcmin
      / 8≤ℓ≤2048). The mock PTEs use the covariance of the matching
      window, with a Hartlap factor on the pure modes only under the
      `monte_carlo`
      [covariance method](#../analyses.covariances.decisions.pure_eb_covariance_method).

decisions:
  fiducial_scale_cuts:
    label: "Scale cuts for the B-mode null tests"
    tags: [scale_cuts]
    rationale: |
      Which angular and multipole ranges the null tests use, the
      ranges Papers III and IV also adopt for inference. The lower
      angular bound sits above the scale of a single MegaCam CCD, so
      it excludes most of the pair separations where the
      [repeating additive bias](#../findings.ccd_scale_cosebi_pattern)
      appears. The cuts were chosen from the B-mode tests together
      with additional systematics checks and blinded
      inference-stability checks in Papers III and IV.

      A cut snaps conservatively to the measurement bins: a θ cut
      keeps the whole reporting bins between its bounds, and an ℓ cut
      keeps the whole bandpowers. Every bin a test uses lies inside
      the stated range, so the tests use slightly less data than the
      range suggests.

      Scale cuts are preferred to subtracting the B modes because
      the relation between E- and B-mode contamination depends on
      the physical mechanism. No look-elsewhere correction is applied
      for the many cuts tested, because the B modes were only one of
      four factors behind the choice, with PSF leakage, modeling
      systematics and the scale-cut dependence of the blinded
      constraints. Treating the two boundaries as fitted parameters
      is the most pessimistic degrees-of-freedom treatment;
      [the finding](#../findings.bmodes_null_at_adopted_cuts) records
      what it does to the PTEs.

      The tables and heatmaps always show both ranges; this decision
      selects which one
      [primary_null_test_report](#outputs.primary_null_test_report)
      treats as primary.
    default: adopted
    options:
      adopted:
        label: "12'–83', 300 < ℓ < 1600"
        insights: [asgari19a_bmode_subtraction_insufficient]
        description: |
          Configuration space: reporting bins 9–15, between edges 9
          and 16 (11.997′ and 82.861′) of the 21-edge
          geomspace(1', 250') reporting grid. Harmonic: the
          bandpowers within 300 < ℓ < 1600.
      full_range:
        label: "Full range (1'–250', 8 ≤ ℓ ≤ 2048)"
        description: |
          Makes the full range the primary report. It is always
          shown beside the fiducial cut in the
          [PTE table](#../outputs.pte_table_appendix) to expose
          contamination at small and large scales.
      bmode_bias_subtraction:
        label: "Subtract a B-mode template"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: |
          The B-mode amplitude does not determine the E-mode
          contamination, since the E/B ratio depends on the
          systematic; scale cuts need no such assumption.
  pte_definition:
    from: ../pte_definition
  pte_threshold:
    label: "PTE pass threshold p_thr"
    tags: [statistics]
    rationale: |
      The test statistic is the minimum PTE over the six B-mode
      statistics, and p_thr is set on the systematics-free GLASS
      realizations so that a clean sample fails 5% of the time, as a
      single test at PTE = 0.05 would. The six are correlated but not
      perfectly, so the minimum skews low and the calibrated p_thr
      sits well below 0.05
      ([mock_min_pte_calibration](#../outputs.mock_min_pte_calibration)).
      It changes little across a wide region of scale cuts around the
      fiducial window
      ([scale-cut scan](#../analyses.validation.analyses.glass_mocks.outputs.mock_min_pte_scale_cut_scan)),
      so a single representative value, rounded conservatively and
      matching the value Paper III uses, is adopted everywhere. A
      [PTE table](#../outputs.pte_table_appendix) row passes when its
      minimum PTE is at least p_thr. This decision sets the heatmap
      colour scale, the threshold marked on the calibration figure
      and the value quoted in the report; the PTEs themselves do not
      depend on it.
    default: calibrated_0p01
    options:
      nominal_0p05:
        label: "0.05 per statistic"
        description: "Each of the six statistics tested against 0.05. The minimum over the six skews low, so a clean sample fails at least one more than 5% of the time."
      calibrated_0p01:
        label: "0.01 on the minimum PTE"
        insights: [asgari19a_bmode_verdict_depends_on_statistic, jefferson25_estimators_disagree_on_same_data]
        description: |
          Conservative rounding of the 350-mock minimum-PTE
          calibration; a clean sample fails it 7% of the time at the
          fiducial cuts.
  scale_cut_pair_grid:
    label: "COSEBI PTE scale-cut grid"
    tags: [scale_cuts]
    rationale: |
      The COSEBI PTE is evaluated for every pair of reporting-grid
      edges, so the [PTE composite figure](#../outputs.fig_pte_heatmaps)
      shows how the verdict depends on the scale cut; its fiducial and
      full-range cells feed the
      [PTE table](#../outputs.pte_table_appendix) and the mock
      calibration. The COSEBI filters T_{±n}(θ) are built from the
      roots of polynomials on the cut interval, a construction that
      becomes numerically unstable as the interval narrows. A pair
      enters the grid only where the filters can be built, because a
      PTE from a failed filter set measures the numerics rather than
      the B modes.
    default: production_grid
    options:
      production_grid:
        label: "Stable index pairs of geomspace(1', 250', 21)"
        description: |
          206 pairs: all 210 edge pairs except the single-bin pairs
          (9, 10), (10, 11), (11, 12) and (13, 14), on which the
          construction of T_{±n}(θ) fails. The figure shows the 190
          cuts that span at least two bins.
      single_pair:
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Full-range PTE reporting and mock calibration require the full-range cell absent from this grid."
        label: "Single pair only (i=9, j=16)"
        description: |
          Only the
          [adopted 12'–83' fiducial cut](#decisions.fiducial_scale_cuts);
          no scale-cut sensitivity.
  fiducial_blind:
    from: ../fiducial_blind
  fiducial_catalog:
    from: ../fiducial_catalog
  leakage_correction:
    from: ../leakage_correction
  reporting_binning:
    from: ../reporting_binning
  reference_covariance:
    from: ../reference_covariance
  integration_grid:
    from: ../integration_grid
  mode_count:
    from: ../mode_count
  mode_subsets:
    label: "PTE-reported mode subsets"
    tags: [estimator]
    rationale: |
      The low-order modes are the cosmologically informative range,
      where the E-mode amplitude has saturated; the full computed
      basis tests the B modes where systematics can still appear,
      which matters for the full-range oscillatory pattern that
      motivates the lower angular cut.
      The selection acts in [primary_null_test_report](#outputs.primary_null_test_report),
      recalibrating its minimum from the selected stored mock PTE columns;
      the complete reference products and mode-vector figures retain both subsets.
      Larger subsets are unavailable because the
      [mode count](#decisions.mode_count) bounds the basis.
    default: n_le_6_and_n_le_20
    options:
      n_le_6_and_n_le_20:
        label: "Both subsets"
        insights: [asgari12_few_cosebis_modes_saturate_information, asgari19a_cosebis_nmax20_for_systematics]
      n_le_6_only:
        label: "n ≤ 6 only"
        description: |
          Drops the n ≤ 20 test.
      n_le_20_only:
        label: "n ≤ 20 only"
        description: |
          Drops the cosmologically informative subset.

prior_insights:

  asgari12_few_cosebis_modes_saturate_information:
    id: asgari12_few_cosebis_modes_saturate_information
    claim: |
      A relatively small number of COSEBI modes always saturates the
      available cosmological information, fewer for logarithmic than
      for linear COSEBIs. Restricting the cosmologically informative
      PTE subset to the first few modes keeps nearly all the E-mode
      information.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/201218828"
        quote:
          exact: "We find that a relatively small number of COSEBIs modes is always enough to saturate to the maximum information level."
        location:
          page: 1
    scope: |
      Fisher forecasts (Asgari, Schneider & Simon 2012); the
      saturation point depends on survey and parameters, and Paper
      II's n ≈ 5–6 comes from its own E-mode data vector.

  asgari19a_cosebis_nmax20_for_systematics:
    id: asgari19a_cosebis_nmax20_for_systematics
    claim: |
      COSEBI E-mode predictions vanish beyond the first ~7 modes, so
      high modes carry no cosmological information, but systematic
      signals need not follow that behaviour and can be significant
      at large n. Truncating at n = 20 covers both the cosmological
      and the systematic-diagnostic range.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/201834379"
        quote:
          exact: "Therefore, we do not expect to gain any cosmological information from these modes."
        location:
          page: 7
      - id: ev2
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/201834379"
        quote:
          exact: "On the other hand the signal from systematic effects does not necessarily follow the same behaviour."
        location:
          page: 7
      - id: ev3
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/201834379"
        quote:
          exact: "which encompasses modes that are important for both cosmological and systematic analyses."
        location:
          page: 7
    scope: |
      COSEBI B-mode analysis of KiDS-450, DES-SV and CFHTLenS
      (Asgari et al. 2019a, §4); same n_max = 20 as Paper II.

  asgari19a_bmode_subtraction_insufficient:
    id: asgari19a_bmode_subtraction_insufficient
    claim: |
      Different systematics contaminate E and B modes by different
      amounts: most produce a significant E-mode contamination on the
      same scales as their B modes, but a repeating additive pattern
      does not. Correcting the data by subtracting the B modes from
      the E modes is therefore not sufficient; the B-mode amplitude
      alone does not determine the E-mode contamination.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/201834379"
        quote:
          exact: "For this reason we have shown that it is not sufficient to correct data by simply subtracting the B-modes from the E-modes."

      fail another computed from the same data, because each weights
      the B modes differently (KiDS-450 passes COSEBIs but shows a
      2.7σ B mode in compressed COSEBIs). The recommendation is to
      require every statistic to be consistent with zero, which is

texts.analyses/validation/astra.yaml:
version: "0.0.14"
name: "Validation"
description: |
  The evidence that the null tests can be trusted. Checks that the results do
  not depend on how the adopted estimators are computed: the pure-mode and COSEBI
  results are remade from a 10,000-bin ξ_± measurement of the fiducial catalog,
  with both grids scored against the 1,000-bin covariance, since no 10,000-bin
  CosmoCov block exists and changing it with the grid would mix the two effects.
  COSEBIs are computed from harmonic-space bandpowers and compared with those
  from ξ_±, which shows that null-test sensitivity is set by the filter functions
  rather than the basis. The B-mode covariances are compared across the n(z)
  blinds, which supports using one blind throughout. The
  [GLASS mocks](#outputs.mock_validation_figure) hold the estimators, covariances and PTE
  convention against 350 systematics-free simulations.

inputs:
  - id: xi_reporting
    from: ../catalog_processing.xi_reporting

  - id: xi_integration
    from: ../catalog_processing.xi_integration

  - id: xi_sweep
    from: ../catalog_processing.xi_sweep

  - id: pure_eb_data
    from: ../catalog_processing.pure_eb_data

  - id: pure_eb_covariance
    from: ../covariances.pure_eb_covariance

  - id: cosebis_covariance
    from: ../covariances.cosebis_covariance

  - id: cosebis_modes_data
    from: ../catalog_processing.cosebis_modes_data

  - id: cl_bandpowers_fine
    from: ../catalog_processing.cl_bandpowers_fine

outputs:
  - id: integration_grid_convergence
    when: [leakage_correction.applied]
    type: data
    format: json
    description: |
      Per reporting bin (ξ_±^B, ξ_±^amb) and per COSEBI mode
      (n = 1 … 20, both scale cuts): the value on the 1,000-bin and
      10,000-bin integration grids, their difference, and that
      difference in units of the fiducial analytic σ, plus the χ²/PTE
      on each grid: the fiducial window (12'–83') for the pure modes,
      both scale cuts at n ≤ 6 and n ≤ 20 for the COSEBIs. For the
      COSEBIs it also carries all four combinations of integration
      grid × COSEBI interval.

      Both grids are scored with the same 1,000-bin covariance: the
      pure-mode matrix
      [pure_eb_covariance](#inputs.pure_eb_covariance)
      and the T^T C_ξ T mode covariance
      [cosebis_covariance](#inputs.cosebis_covariance). Both grids
      are TreeCorr runs over the same catalog on the same
      [0.5', 300'] extent, so sample variance cancels and every
      difference is numerical.
      This cross-check is available only for corrected shear: the
      10,000-bin measurement exists only for the leak-corrected catalog.

      Sanity checks: pair counts summed into each reporting bin on
      both grids (totals agree to 4e-6; per-bin sums differ because
      the one fine bin straddling each reporting edge is assigned
      whole, up to 3.0% of a reporting bin at 1,000 bins and 0.3% at
      10,000), and the effective COSEBI interval each grid's
      bin selection produces. The fiducial window is bins (9, 15)
      on both grids.
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, pure_eb_integration_method, pure_eb_rebinning_weights, pure_eb_integration_limits, mode_count, decomposition_method, pte_definition, leakage_correction, reporting_binning, integration_grid]
    inputs: [xi_reporting, xi_integration, xi_10000_bins, pure_eb_data, pure_eb_covariance, cosebis_modes_data, cosebis_covariance]

        --xi-1k {inputs.xi_integration}
        --xi-10k {inputs.xi_10000_bins}
        --pure-eb-baseline {inputs.pure_eb_data}
        --pure-eb-covariance {inputs.pure_eb_covariance}

        --cosebis-covariance {inputs.cosebis_covariance}

findings:

  pure_modes_converged_at_1000_bins:
    label: "Pure modes converged at 1,000 bins"
    claim: |
      The adopted pure-mode chain is converged on the 1,000-bin
      integration grid: refining to 10,000 bins leaves the
      fiducial-window PTEs essentially unchanged, and the coherent
      positive ξ_-^B offset that drives the window's ξ_-^B PTE is not
      a grid artifact.
    notes: |
      Refining to 10,000 bins moves ξ_±^B by at most 0.13 σ in any of
      the seven fiducial-window bins (0.35 σ over all 20 bins, in the
      168' bin near the operator's upper edge) and the ambiguous modes
      by at most 0.054 σ anywhere. PTEs: ξ_+^B 0.823 → 0.837, ξ_-^B
      0.0193 → 0.0216, joint 0.0387 → 0.0430. The residual per-bin
      motion is sign-alternating, not coherent.
    created_at: "2026-09-13T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: integration_grid_convergence
        quote:
          exact: '"pte": 0.837078570047477'

  cosebis_verdicts_stable_at_1000_bins:
    label: "COSEBI B_n and their significance stable on a 10,000-bin grid"
    claim: |
      Repeating the COSEBI calculation on a 10,000-bin grid for the
      fiducial catalog finds the B_n amplitudes and their significance
      to be stable: with each grid on its own bin selection, the n ≤ 6
      modes move by at most 0.76 σ and no PTE verdict changes, while
      individual higher modes (n ≥ 10) shift by up to 1.41 σ.
    notes: |
      n ≤ 6 shifts are at most 0.56 σ at the fiducial cuts and
      0.76 σ over the full range. PTEs: fiducial n ≤ 6 0.777 → 0.759,
      n ≤ 20 0.943 → 0.789; full range n ≤ 6 1.37×10⁻⁵ → 1.07×10⁻⁵,
      n ≤ 20 1.08×10⁻⁴ → 2.76×10⁻⁴. Individual higher modes move by up
      to 1.41 σ at the fiducial cuts and 1.23 σ over the full range.

      Each grid's edge-based bin selection lands on a slightly
      different θ interval (12.053′–82.141′ at 1,000 bins,
      12.003′–82.800′ at 10,000), so the comparison above changes
      interval and resolution together. Recomputing each grid over
      the other's interval, as closely as its nodes allow, moves the
      n ≤ 6 modes by up to 0.73 σ at the fiducial cuts and 1.13 σ
      over the full range, and any mode by up to 1.24 σ and 1.13 σ.
      Fiducial PTEs stay within 0.60–0.93; full-range PTEs rise to
      6.4×10⁻⁴–1.77×10⁻³ (n ≤ 6) and 0.011 (n ≤ 20, just above
      the 0.01 threshold, though n ≤ 6 still fails). Shifts are in
      units of the 1,000-bin σ (the only mode covariance), not a
      significance of the difference.
    created_at: "2026-09-13T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: integration_grid_convergence
        quote:
          exact: '"pte": 0.7593239449047392'

        --fiducial-cl-cov-path "$k/cl_cov_$ver"_blind=A_powspace_nbins=$nb.fits \
        --fiducial-xi-path "$x/$ver"_xi_minsep=0.5_maxsep=300.0_nbins=1000_npatch=1.txt \
        --fiducial-cov-path "$c/$cb/$cb"_processed.txt \
        --out-file {output}
      rm -rf "$x" "$c" "$l" "$k"
    resources:
      cpus: 8
      memory: 16GB
  format: npz
- id: cosebis_harmonic_version_ptes
  type: metric
  description: |
    Harmonic- and configuration-path COSEBI B-mode χ² and PTEs over
    n ≤ 6 for the 3 non-fiducial catalog versions, at the
    fiducial and full angular ranges. Supplies those versions'
    harmonic rows in the
    [harmonic/configuration COSEBI table](#../../outputs.cosebis_harmonic_config);
    the fiducial version's rows come from
    [cosebis_harmonic_metrics](#../outputs.cosebis_harmonic_metrics)
    and
    [cosebis_harmonic_metrics_full](#../outputs.cosebis_harmonic_metrics_full).
  inputs:
  - harmonic_modes_sp_v1p4p5
  - harmonic_modes_sp_v1p4p8
  - harmonic_modes_sp_v1p4p11p3
  recipe:

      python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/merge_harmonic_version_ptes.py --members {inputs.harmonic_modes_sp_v1p4p5} {inputs.harmonic_modes_sp_v1p4p8} {inputs.harmonic_modes_sp_v1p4p11p3} --out-file {output}
    resources:
      cpus: 1
      memory: 4GB
  format: json
texts.analyses/validation/analyses/glass_mocks:
version: "0.0.14"
name: "GLASS mocks"
description: |
  Validation of the B-mode estimators, covariances and PTE
  convention on 350 systematics-free GLASS lognormal realizations.
  The realizations contain no B-mode signal, so every B statistic
  they produce is noise: their scatter is the empirical σ to hold
  the analytic σ against, their per-mock χ² values test the PTE
  convention and calibrate the min-PTE threshold, and their χ²
  correlations measure how independent the six statistics are.

  Each realization is measured independently (the
  [ξ_± ensemble](#inputs.glass_mock_xi_fine)) and carried through the
  same ξ_± → COSEBI and ξ_± → pure-E/B transforms the data use; all
  six statistics are then compared against analytic covariances.
  The key [decision](#decisions.reference_covariance) is which
  covariance, and it follows the [suite](#decisions.mock_suite). A
  suite matched to the data's footprint, count and σ_e is held against
  the data's own covariances, so the campaign tests the covariance the
  null tests use. A suite sampled differently, as the published
  v1.4.6.3_v2 suite is
  ([mocks_are_over_constraining](#findings.mocks_are_over_constraining)),
  is held against a covariance the same CosmoCov and NaMaster chain
  builds at the suite's own noise, and the campaign tests the
  covariance machinery. Either way the
  [analytic covariances](#../../analyses.covariances.outputs.pure_eb_covariance_reference), not a mock sample
  covariance, enter the PTEs.

inputs:

  - id: glass_mock_xi_fine
    from: ../glass_mock_xi_fine

  - id: glass_mock_xi_reporting
    from: ../glass_mock_xi_reporting

  - id: glass_mock_cl
    from: ../glass_mock_cl

  - id: glass_mock_sampling
    from: ../glass_mock_sampling

  - id: glass_mock_realization_00001
    from: ../glass_mock_realization_00001

  - id: xi_integration
    from: ../xi_integration

  - id: cl_cov_reporting
    from: ../cl_cov_reporting

  - id: cov_integration_reference
    from: ../cov_integration_reference

  - id: cov_reporting_reference
    from: ../cov_reporting_reference

  - id: cl_cov_reference
    from: ../cl_cov_reference

  - id: pure_eb_covariance_reference
    from: ../pure_eb_covariance_reference

  - id: redshift_distributions
    from: ../redshift_distributions

  - id: survey_areas
    from: ../survey_areas

  - id: cosmology_snapshot
    from: ../cosmology_snapshot

outputs:

  # ── The per-realization data vectors ─────────────────────────────────────

  - id: mock_cosebis_modes
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      COSEBI E_n / B_n for n = 1 … 20 and all 350 realizations, stacked
      as a 350 × 20 pair, computed from
      [glass_mock_xi_fine](#inputs.glass_mock_xi_fine) with the same
      `cosmo_numba` call as the data vector, over the
      [fiducial θ range](#../../analyses.significance.decisions.fiducial_scale_cuts). The
      filters span the first and last fine-bin centres inside the cut,
      12.05′–82.14′.
      [mock_cosebis_modes_full](#outputs.mock_cosebis_modes_full) is
      the 1–250 arcmin counterpart.
    inputs: [glass_mock_xi_fine]
    decisions: [mock_suite]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/mock_cosebis_scatter.py
        --xi-ensemble {inputs.glass_mock_xi_fine} --out-file {output}
        --nmodes 20
      resources: { cpus: 16, memory: "8GB" }

  - id: mock_cosebis_modes_full
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      Full-range COSEBI E_n / B_n for n = 1 … 20 and all 350
      realizations, stacked as a 350 × 20 pair: as
      [mock_cosebis_modes](#outputs.mock_cosebis_modes), over the
      1–250 arcmin range of the full-range data PTEs.
    inputs: [glass_mock_xi_fine]
    decisions: [mock_suite]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/mock_cosebis_scatter.py
        --xi-ensemble {inputs.glass_mock_xi_fine} --out-file {output}
        --nmodes 20 --theta-min 1.0 --theta-max 250.0
      resources: { cpus: 16, memory: "8GB" }

  - id: mock_pure_eb_modes
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      Pure-mode ξ_±^{E,B,amb} for all 350 realizations on the 20-bin
      reporting grid, stacked as six 350 × 20 blocks. The reporting
      bins come from
      [glass_mock_xi_reporting](#inputs.glass_mock_xi_reporting) and the transform
      runs over [glass_mock_xi_fine](#inputs.glass_mock_xi_fine), on the same
      0.5′–300′ grid as the data, under the same
      [quadrature](#decisions.pure_eb_integration_method). Under
      `npairs` [weights](#decisions.pure_eb_rebinning_weights) each
      realization is averaged with its own pair counts.
    inputs: [glass_mock_xi_fine, glass_mock_xi_reporting]
    decisions: [mock_suite, pure_eb_integration_method, pure_eb_rebinning_weights, pure_eb_integration_limits, decomposition_method]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/mock_pure_eb_scatter.py
        --fine-ensemble {inputs.glass_mock_xi_fine}
        --reporting-ensemble {inputs.glass_mock_xi_reporting}
        --integration-method {decisions.pure_eb_integration_method}
        --rebinning-weights {decisions.pure_eb_rebinning_weights}
        --integration-limits {decisions.pure_eb_integration_limits}
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 16, memory: "16GB" }

  # ── The six-statistic campaign ───────────────────────────────────────────

  - id: mock_per_mock_statistics
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      Per-realization results for the six statistics (B_{n≤6},
      B_{n≤20}, ξ_+^B, ξ_-^B, ξ_tot^B, C_ℓ^BB): each realization's B
      vector and its χ² and PTE against the selected reference
      covariance, at the fiducial cuts and over the full range
      (`chi2_full`, `pte_full`, `dof_full`; 1–250 arcmin / 8≤ℓ≤2048).
      Also carries the analytic σ vectors on both ranges, the cut
      masks, and the covariance triple, scale cuts and any skipped
      realizations. The campaign's σ, χ² and PTE summaries derive from
      this file.
    inputs: [mock_cosebis_modes, mock_cosebis_modes_full, mock_pure_eb_modes, glass_mock_xi_fine, glass_mock_cl, xi_integration, cov_integration_reference, pure_eb_covariance_reference, cl_cov_reference]
    decisions: [reference_covariance, mock_suite, fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, pte_definition, integration_grid]
    recipe:
      command: >
        c=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.glass_mock_cl} -C $c &&
        python src/workflow/scripts/mock_campaign_analysis.py
        --cosebis-ensemble {inputs.mock_cosebis_modes}
        --cosebis-ensemble-full {inputs.mock_cosebis_modes_full}
        --pure-ensemble {inputs.mock_pure_eb_modes}
        --fine-ensemble {inputs.glass_mock_xi_fine}
        --cl-dir "$c"
        --cosebis-xi-grid {inputs.xi_integration}
        --cosebis-cov {inputs.cov_integration_reference}
        --pure-cov {inputs.pure_eb_covariance_reference}
        --cl-cov {inputs.cl_cov_reference}
        --label {decisions.reference_covariance}
        --emit-stats {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: mock_min_pte_scale_cut_scan
    type: data
    format: json
    description: |
      [mock_min_pte_calibration](#../../analyses.significance.outputs.mock_min_pte_calibration) as
      a function of the scale cut: the same 5%-quantile threshold on
      the per-realization minimum PTE, evaluated on all 210 windows of
      the reporting grid `geomspace(1', 250', 21)` rather than at the
      fiducial window alone. Per window it carries θ_min, θ_max, the
      threshold, its 68% bootstrap and order-statistic intervals, the
      median minimum PTE, the false-alarm rates at 0.01 and 0.05, the
      six per-statistic median PTEs, the number of reporting bins, and
      the reasons any statistic could not be formed.

      The COSEBIs are recomputed in each window from each
      realization's [fine ξ_±](#inputs.glass_mock_xi_fine), against a COSEBI
      covariance transformed on that window; holding them at their
      fiducial values would depress the threshold across the plane.
      C_ℓ^BB does not depend on the angular window, so its PTEs come
      unchanged from
      [mock_per_mock_statistics](#outputs.mock_per_mock_statistics).

      The windows are the reporting grid's own bin edges, so the
      fiducial cell (edge indices 9, 16) is the window
      [mock_min_pte_calibration](#../../analyses.significance.outputs.mock_min_pte_calibration)
      calibrates at; the two thresholds agree to machine precision.

      The 20 single-bin windows are marked `comparable: false` and
      excluded from summaries: the COSEBI basis is too ill-conditioned
      over one reporting bin. On the 190 windows of two bins or more,
      the calibrated threshold lies below the adopted
      [p_thr = 0.01](#../../analyses.significance.decisions.pte_threshold)
      on 119 in `baseline` (141 in `published`); the excursions at the
      plane's extremes come from few, highly correlated degrees of
      freedom at small θ and the known large-scale contamination at
      large θ_max.
    inputs: [mock_per_mock_statistics, glass_mock_xi_fine, mock_pure_eb_modes, xi_integration, cov_integration_reference, pure_eb_covariance_reference]
    decisions: [reference_covariance, mock_suite, pte_definition, integration_grid]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/min_pte_window_scan.py
        --per-mock-statistics {inputs.mock_per_mock_statistics}
        --mock-xi-fine {inputs.glass_mock_xi_fine}
        --mock-pure-eb-modes {inputs.mock_pure_eb_modes}
        --cosebis-xi-grid {inputs.xi_integration}
        --covariance {inputs.cov_integration_reference}
        --pure-covariance {inputs.pure_eb_covariance_reference}
        --reference-covariance {decisions.reference_covariance}
        --xi-min-sep 0.5 --xi-max-sep 300.0 --xi-nbins 1000
        --reporting-theta-min 1.0 --reporting-theta-max 250.0 --reporting-edges 21
        --fiducial-window 9 16
        --nmodes 20 --precision 120 --global-alpha 0.05
        --cosebi-roots interpolate_ratio
        --processes 24
        --emit calibration --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 24, memory: "32GB" }

  - id: mock_campaign_evidence
    type: data
    format: json
    description: |
      The campaign's summary statistics, derived from
      [mock_per_mock_statistics](#outputs.mock_per_mock_statistics):
      per statistic, σ_emp/σ_ana, mean χ², PTE uniformity tests and the
      cross-statistic correlations. The σ-ratio, χ² and correlation
      numbers in the findings are read from it.

      Covariance conventions per statistic: COSEBIs transform the ξ_±
      covariance with no Hartlap factor; the pure-mode blocks are
      sliced from the stored 120×120 matrix, with a Hartlap factor only
      under the `monte_carlo`
      [covariance method](#../../analyses.covariances.decisions.pure_eb_covariance_method), where
      N is its 2000 draws; C_ℓ^BB takes
      no Hartlap factor, its reference being
      [cl_cov_reference](#inputs.cl_cov_reference). Pure-mode σ is
      reported on all 20 reporting bins and on the fiducial cut, COSEBI
      σ on the fiducial window and C_ℓ^BB σ on the 17 fiducial bands.
    inputs: [mock_per_mock_statistics]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/mock_campaign_analysis.py
        --from-stats {inputs.mock_per_mock_statistics}
        --emit evidence --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "4GB" }

  - id: mock_sigma_ratio_figure
    type: figure
    format: pdf
    description: |
      Empirical σ over analytic σ, per COSEBI mode on the fiducial
      window, per θ bin for ξ_±^B, and per ℓ band for the 17 fiducial
      C_ℓ^BB bands, with the fiducial cut shaded. Against a reference
      covariance at the suite's own noise it tests the analytic
      covariance amplitude; against one at a different noise it also
      carries the noise mismatch.
    inputs: [mock_per_mock_statistics]
    decisions: [reference_covariance]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/mock_campaign_analysis.py
        --from-stats {inputs.mock_per_mock_statistics}
        --emit sigma-ratio-figure --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "4GB" }

  - id: mock_validation_figure
    type: figure
    format: png
    description: |
      The paper's mock-validation figure, over every reporting bin of
      the three B statistics — COSEBI modes 1–20 (at the fiducial cuts,
      filled, and over 1–250′, open), ξ_+^B (filled) and ξ_-^B (open)
      on all reporting bins, C_ℓ^BB on all 32 bands — with scales
      outside the fiducial cuts shaded. Top row: across-realization
      mean in units of the analytic σ of the
      [reference covariance](#decisions.reference_covariance), with
      σ_emp/(σ_ana√N) error bars. Bottom row: σ_ana/σ_emp (below one
      means the analytic σ is tighter than the mock scatter), with
      ±1/√(2N) error bars; the lowest C_ℓ band (≈1.8) is dropped from
      this row only.

      Outside the cuts the analytic covariance degrades: σ_ana/σ_emp
      rises to ≈1.8 at the lowest bandpower and returns to unity only
      by ℓ ≈ 100, falls from 0.85–0.88 at 127′ to ≈0.77 at 221′ in
      configuration space, and sits at 0.77–0.85 for the full-range
      COSEBI modes n ≤ 6. Inside the cuts every ratio is within ~15%
      of unity and every mean bias below 0.12σ. The full 32-band C_ℓ
      stack is read from
      [glass_mock_cl](#inputs.glass_mock_cl), since
      [mock_per_mock_statistics](#outputs.mock_per_mock_statistics)
      stores only the in-cut bands.
    inputs: [mock_per_mock_statistics, mock_campaign_evidence, glass_mock_cl]
    decisions: [reference_covariance, mock_suite]
    recipe:
      command: >
        c=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.glass_mock_cl} -C $c &&
        python src/workflow/scripts/mock_validation_figure.py
        --per-mock-statistics {inputs.mock_per_mock_statistics}
        --campaign-evidence {inputs.mock_campaign_evidence}
        --cl-dir "$c"
        --range full
        --output {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "4GB" }

  # ── The raw ξ_± check, upstream of every mode filter ─────────────────────

  - id: mock_xi_input_theory
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      The theory ξ_± the GLASS suite was generated from, on its
      reporting grid, rebuilt with CAMB under the generator's setup:
      the [cosmology snapshot](#inputs.cosmology_snapshot)'s Planck-18
      values, HMcode `mead2020_feedback` at log T_AGN = 7.8, A_s
      rescaled to σ_8 = 0.8102, and the fiducial
      [n(z)](#inputs.redshift_distributions).

      The transform is an explicit Bessel sum band-limited at the
      simulation's ℓ_max = NSide = 4096. An FFTLog transform would
      extrapolate past the last multipole and restore power the maps
      lack, which matters because ξ_- at 1′ is built almost entirely
      from ℓ ~ 10⁴. The unbanded transform (`xip_untruncated` /
      `xim_untruncated`) and the curved-sky FFTLog result are written
      alongside.
    inputs: [glass_mock_xi_reporting, cosmology_snapshot, redshift_distributions]
    decisions: [mock_suite]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/mock_xi_input_theory.py
        --cosmology-json {inputs.cosmology_snapshot}
        --reporting-ensemble {inputs.glass_mock_xi_reporting}
        --cat-config src/cosmo_val/cat_config.yaml
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 8, memory: "32GB" }

  - id: mock_xi_validation_figure
    type: figure
    format: png
    description: |
      Validation of the raw 20-bin ξ_± before any pure-mode or COSEBI
      filter. Row 1: θξ_±, the across-realization mean against
      [the input theory](#outputs.mock_xi_input_theory), band-limited
      at the simulation's ℓ_max and unbanded. Row 2: (mean −
      theory)/σ_ana, a fraction of a single realization's error bar,
      with σ_emp/(σ_ana√N) error bars as in
      [mock_validation_figure](#outputs.mock_validation_figure). Row
      3: σ_emp/σ_ana. σ_ana comes from the
      [reference covariance](#inputs.cov_reporting_reference).
      Scales outside the fiducial 12–83′ cut are shaded.

      Above ≈6′ the mock mean reproduces the input theory to a few per
      cent with no trend; below it the drop of ξ_- (a factor ~100 at
      1′) is reproduced bin for bin by band-limiting the theory at
      ℓ = 4096, the simulation's resolution, wholly outside the
      fiducial cut.
    inputs: [glass_mock_xi_reporting, mock_xi_input_theory, cov_reporting_reference]
    decisions: [mock_suite]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/mock_xi_validation.py
        --reporting-ensemble {inputs.glass_mock_xi_reporting}
        --theory {inputs.mock_xi_input_theory}
        --covariance {inputs.cov_reporting_reference}
        --emit figure --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "4GB" }

  - id: mock_xi_validation_stats
    type: data
    format: json
    description: |
      The numbers behind
      [mock_xi_validation_figure](#outputs.mock_xi_validation_figure),
      per reporting bin: mean ξ_± over theory, the residual in
      units of a single realization's σ_ana and in units of
      σ_emp/√N, σ_emp, σ_ana and their ratio. Two further columns:

      - The shape-noise σ implied by the measured pair counts,
        σ_e²/√(2N_pair). The total σ over it rises from 1.0 at 1′ to 4.2 at
        221′ for raw ξ_+ as sample variance takes over, so shape noise
        is only 5.7% of the ξ_+ variance at 221′ and the footprint pair
        deficit moves σ by about 1% or less at every separation.
      - The galaxy count each bin's pair count implies for a
        uniform-density footprint of the fiducial area: 1.02 of the
        delivered count at 1′, falling monotonically to 0.87 at 221′ as
        annuli run off the footprint edge — the geometry effect the
        pure-mode scatter inherits at large θ.
    inputs: [glass_mock_xi_reporting, mock_xi_input_theory, cov_reporting_reference, survey_areas, glass_mock_sampling, glass_mock_realization_00001]
    decisions: [mock_suite, fiducial_catalog]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/mock_xi_validation.py
        --reporting-ensemble {inputs.glass_mock_xi_reporting}
        --theory {inputs.mock_xi_input_theory}
        --covariance {inputs.cov_reporting_reference}
        --survey-properties {decisions.fiducial_catalog}
        --sampling {inputs.glass_mock_sampling}
        --realization-summary {inputs.glass_mock_realization_00001}
        --emit stats --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "2GB" }

  - id: mock_mean_vector_stats
    type: data
    format: json
    description: |
      Per-statistic mean B across the realizations, averaged over
      scales, raw and in units of the analytic σ, with its standard
      error and z-score, and the largest absolute normalised mean with
      the mode or bin it falls in.

      The mean-vector χ², against the empirical covariance of the mean,
      is quoted on the full 20-bin reporting grid (`full_range`) and,
      for the pure modes, on the fiducial bins 9–15
      (`fiducial_window`); COSEBIs and C_ℓ^BB carry `full_range` alone,
      over their 20 modes and 17 fiducial bands. For the pure modes the
      two differ: ⟨ξ_+^B⟩
      sits at ≈−0.1σ in the first three bins against a ≈0.055σ error,
      a small-scale residual the cut excludes, so ξ_+^B reads PTE 0.004
      on the full range and 0.13 inside the cut.
    inputs: [mock_per_mock_statistics]
    decisions: [reference_covariance, pte_definition, reporting_binning]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/mock_mean_vector_plot.py
        --stats {inputs.mock_per_mock_statistics}
        --label {decisions.reference_covariance}
        --reporting-binning {decisions.reporting_binning}
        --emit stats --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "2GB" }

  - id: clbb_variance_ratios
    type: data
    format: json
    description: |
      The measured mock-to-data C_ℓ^BB variance ratio over the 17
      bandpowers inside 300 ≤ ℓ ≤ 1600, two ways. The machinery ratio
      is the diagonal of the
      [reference covariance](#inputs.cl_cov_reference) over that of
      the data's [cl_cov_reporting](#inputs.cl_cov_reporting): what the
      covariance chain predicts at the reference's noise, unity under
      `data_covariance` by construction. The empirical ratio is the
      sample variance of the suite's BB bandpowers
      ([glass_mock_cl](#inputs.glass_mock_cl)) over the same data
      diagonal. With no B signal, both are noise-dominated ratios.
      Mean, median and per-band values. For a suite with the data's
      noise the empirical ratio tests the data's C_ℓ^BB covariance
      directly; for one sampled differently it measures the noise
      difference the [reference covariance](#decisions.reference_covariance)
      must follow.
    inputs: [cl_cov_reference, cl_cov_reporting, glass_mock_cl]
    decisions: [mock_suite, fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind]
    recipe:
      command: >
        c=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.glass_mock_cl} -C $c &&
        python src/workflow/scripts/clbb_variance_ratios.py
        --cl-cov-reference {inputs.cl_cov_reference}
        --cl-cov-data {inputs.cl_cov_reporting}
        --cl-files "$c/cl_glass_mock_*_4096.npy"
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "4GB" }

    from: ../../integration_grid
  pte_definition:

  decomposition_method:

prior_insights:

  paper_iv_inka_overestimates_variance:
    id: paper_iv_inka_overestimates_variance
    label: "Paper IV's iNKA covariance overestimates the small-scale variance"
    claim: |
      The Gaussian iNKA covariance adopted by UNIONS Paper IV
      (harmonic-space cosmology) gives larger small-scale
      uncertainties than either `OneCovariance` or the GLASS mocks —
      around 20% against both, with its Fig. 4 caption quoting 15%
      against the mocks — and Paper IV attributes the gap to iNKA accounting for a spatially
      varying galaxy number density, which breaks the stationary-noise
      assumption the other two estimates make.
    notes: |
      The same GLASS suite is on the other side of that comparison and
      is under-noised by a comparable factor; the two effects add (see
      [mocks_are_over_constraining](#findings.mocks_are_over_constraining)).
    created_at: "2026-08-29T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev_main_text
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.2605.13543"
        quote:
          exact: "However, the estimate computed from the Gaussian part of iNKA tends to overestimate the variance."
        location: { page: 6 }
      - id: ev_caption_15
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.2605.13543"
        quote:
          exact: "There is a discrepancy of 15% between the NaMaster estimate and the one obtained from mocks."
        location: { page: 6 }
      - id: ev_appendix_20
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.2605.13543"
        quote:
          exact: "the iNKA covariance used in this work overestimates by around 20% the uncertainty compared to what is obtained from OneCovariance and GLASS simulations"
        location: { page: 14 }
      - id: ev_mechanism
        doi: "10.48550/arXiv.2605.13543"
        quote:

        location: { page: 14 }


findings:

  mock_xi_matches_input_theory_above_band_limit:
    id: mock_xi_matches_input_theory_above_band_limit
    label: "Mock ξ_± matches input theory above the band limit"
    claim: |
      Above ≈6′ the across-realization mean ξ_± of the GLASS
      realizations reproduces the theory the suite was generated from
      to within a few per cent with no trend, so the mocks carry no
      ξ_± bias into the null tests. Below ≈6′ they depart from the
      unbanded prediction, ξ_- falling away by up to two orders of
      magnitude and ξ_+ ringing by up to 15%, because the maps are
      band-limited at ℓ_max = NSide = 4096; these scales lie outside
      the fiducial cut.
    notes: |
      350 realizations. Inside the 12′–83′ window |mean/theory − 1| ≤
      0.03 for ξ_+ and ≤ 0.04 for ξ_-; bin by bin |mean − theory| ≤ 0.33
      σ_ana (ξ_+) and ≤ 0.46 σ_ana (ξ_-) against an error of the mean
      of ≈0.05 σ_ana, scattered in sign. That is the size of the
      band-limited transform's own ±2–4% ringing (2% of ξ_+ at 18′ is
      0.30 σ_ana); against the unbanded prediction the same mean agrees
      to 1.6% (ξ_+) and 0.7% (ξ_-). So it bounds a mock ξ_± bias at a
      third to a half of an error bar rather than measuring one.

      Below ≈6′: the mock ξ_- at 1.2′ is ≈2% of the unbanded prediction,
      since ξ_-(1′) is built almost entirely from ℓ ~ 10⁴.
      Over the first six reporting bins the theory's band ratio (cut at
      ℓ = 4096) runs 0.006, 0.020, 0.071, 0.166, 0.400, 0.815, against a
      measured mock mean over unbanded theory of −0.021, 0.002, 0.099,
      0.202, 0.463, 0.828 — tracking across two orders of magnitude,
      with the mocks 2–40% above the sharp cut over the last four bins,
      as lognormal small-scale power and an imperfectly sharp band edge
      would give. This is why
      [mock_xi_input_theory](#outputs.mock_xi_input_theory) is an
      explicit band-limited sum: an FFTLog that extrapolates past the
      last multipole makes the same comparison look like a
      catastrophic small-scale failure. Any use of this suite below
      ≈6′, in ξ_- especially, measures the band limit.
    created_at: "2026-09-13T00:00:00Z"
    derived: true
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: mock_xi_validation_stats
      - id: ev2
        artifact: mock_xi_validation_figure

  mock_xi_scatter_falls_below_analytic_at_large_theta:
    id: mock_xi_scatter_falls_below_analytic_at_large_theta
    label: "Mock ξ_+ scatter falls below analytic σ above 100′"
    claim: |
      Against the
      [mock-matched reference covariance](#inputs.cov_reporting_reference),
      the mocks' raw ξ_± scatter matches the analytic Gaussian σ inside
      the fiducial window, but above 100′ the ξ_+ scatter falls below
      it while ξ_- stays near unity. The deficit is neither a density
      nor a footprint effect, and reads as the realizations carrying
      less large-scale sample variance than the analytic covariance
      predicts — a reading of the residual, not an established
      mechanism.
    notes: |
      In the data-matched `baseline` suite against the data's Gaussian
      covariance, σ_emp/σ_ana inside 12′–83′ reads 0.91–1.09 (ξ_+) and
      1.00–1.06 (ξ_-); above 96′ ξ_- sits at 1.02–1.09 and ξ_+ at
      0.86–0.93.

      Not footprint geometry: at 221′ the implied galaxy count is 13%
      low, a 24% pair deficit, but shape noise is only a small share of
      the ξ_+ variance there, so it moves σ by about 1% or less at
      every separation. ξ_+ above 100′ draws on the lowest multipoles,
      where a lognormal shell construction on a single footprint is
      least trusted.

      The pair counts themselves fall away from the uniform-density,
      no-edge prediction: the implied galaxy count per bin declines
      monotonically from 1.02 of the delivered count at 1′ to 0.87 at
      221′ (both suites). That decline (not its absolute level, which
      floats with the area convention) is the footprint-edge effect the
      noise-only pure-mode statistics inherit at large θ; it is
      invisible in raw ξ_± for the reason above.
    created_at: "2026-09-13T00:00:00Z"
    derived: true
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: mock_xi_validation_stats

  mocks_are_over_constraining:
    id: mocks_are_over_constraining
    label: "The v1.4.6.3_v2 suite's galaxy density is 17% above the data's"
    claim: |
      Because of an error in the catalog generation, the galaxy number
      density of the published v1.4.6.3_v2 GLASS realizations is 17%
      higher than the data's, so their shape noise and B-mode scatter
      are lower. Scatter from that suite is therefore compared only
      against analytic covariances recomputed at the realizations'
      galaxy density, whereas the data-matched `baseline` suite is held
      directly against the data covariances.
    notes: |
      **Size.** The `v1.4.6.3_v2` suite samples 6.0905 arcmin⁻²
      unit-weight galaxies on the 2757.25 deg² of occupied v1.4.6
      pixels, about 60.4 M per realization, against the fiducial
      catalog's 51.65 M weight-effective galaxies on the same sky, with
      per-component σ_e 0.2684 against the data's 0.2676. The count
      ratio is nearly the whole noise difference, and a pure-noise
      B-mode variance scales as its square. Measured as 17-band means
      over 300 ≤ ℓ ≤ 1600
      ([clbb_variance_ratios](#outputs.clbb_variance_ratios)): in
      `published` the covariance machinery at the suite's noise gives a
      C_ℓ^BB variance ratio of 0.728 of the data's, and the 350
      realizations scatter at 0.706. In the data-matched `baseline`
      suite the machinery ratio is 1.000 by construction and the 350
      realizations scatter at 0.967 of the data covariance.

      **Origin.** The generator (`make_unions_glass_sim.py`) defaults
      `--neff` to 6.0905 arcmin⁻², a catalog n_eff from the earlier
      2405 deg² area (the fiducial catalog's is 4.957 on 2894 deg²),
      and the run scripts do not override it. It applies that density to an
      occupied-pixel nside-4096 mask of 2757.25 deg²: 6.0905 × 2757.25 ×
      3600 = 60.45 M, against 60.27–60.42 M realised per realization.
      The catalog's A = 2894.03 deg² is the full footprint mask, in
      which roughly 5% of pixels hold no galaxy; data galaxies occupy
      2750.65 deg² of it, so n_eff × A, not n_eff, is the comparable
      quantity. Paper III and Paper IV describe the mocks as
      matching the data's number density; neither prints a numeric
      mock density, and Sacha Guerrini has confirmed the excess.

      **Paper IV.** Paper IV finds its Gaussian iNKA covariance
      overestimates the small-scale variance relative to the GLASS
      mocks and `OneCovariance` (~20% against both; its Fig. 4 caption
      quotes 15% against the mocks), attributing it to iNKA's
      treatment of a spatially varying number density
      ([paper_iv_inka_overestimates_variance](#prior_insights.paper_iv_inka_overestimates_variance)).
      The density excess makes the `v1.4.6.3_v2` mocks' variance ~27%
      low by construction, an independent contribution in the same
      direction; part of that gap is plausibly the mocks being
      under-noised. The two effects are additive and nothing here
      quantifies the split.
    created_at: "2026-08-29T00:00:00Z"
    derived: true
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: clbb_variance_ratios
      - id: ev2
        artifact: mock_sigma_ratio_figure
    scope: "The published GLASS v1.4.6.3_v2 suite against the v1.4.6.3 leak-corrected fiducial catalog (`published` machinery/empirical 0.728/0.706; data-matched `baseline` 1.000/0.967)."

  covariance_amplitude_validated:
    id: covariance_amplitude_validated
    label: "Analytic σ matches the mock scatter at the fiducial cuts"
    claim: |
      At the fiducial cuts the analytic σ of each B-mode statistic
      matches the scatter across the realizations, slightly smaller in
      configuration space and in agreement in harmonic space. The
      agreement degrades on large scales outside the fiducial cuts,
      which PSF leakage already excludes (Paper I), so the
      miscalibration does not affect the choice of scale cuts.
    notes: |
      In the data-matched `baseline` suite held directly against the
      data covariances, as σ_emp/σ_ana (the inverse of the paper's
      σ_ana/σ_emp ratio): COSEBI B_1–B_20 median 1.041 (range
      0.938–1.115); ξ_+^B over the seven fiducial-cut θ bins median
      1.099 (0.997–1.146); ξ_-^B median 1.031 (0.971–1.062); C_ℓ^BB
      over the 17 fiducial-cut bands median 0.981 (0.934–1.056).
      Inverted, these are σ_ana/σ_emp = 0.96, 0.91, 0.97 and 1.02
      (against 0.94, 0.90, 0.95 and 1.03 in `published`).

      Outside the cuts the analytic σ is about 13–17% too small for the
      first COSEBI mode and for ξ_±^B above 100′, and too large for
      C_ℓ^BB below ℓ ≈ 100, where E-to-B leakage is treated only
      approximately (Nicola et al. 2021). Because `baseline` compares
      against the data's own covariances directly, it validates the
      covariances entering the null tests, not just the covariance
      machinery.
    created_at: "2026-08-29T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: mock_campaign_evidence
        quote:
          exact: '"median": 1.0407183334974905'
      - id: ev2
        artifact: mock_campaign_evidence
        quote:
          exact: '"median": 0.9812997317220769'
    scope: "350 data-matched GLASS realizations against the data covariances (`baseline`), fiducial scale cuts (with `published` v1.4.6.3_v2 values noted)."

  chi2_machinery_conservative:
    id: chi2_machinery_conservative
    label: "The null tests are conservative"
    claim: |
      The null tests use only the Gaussian part of the covariance,
      which underestimates the true variances by omitting connected
      trispectrum and super-sample terms. They are therefore
      conservative: a test that passes with the Gaussian-only
      covariance would generally pass with a more complete covariance
      estimate, as the simulations confirm.
    notes: |
      The non-Gaussian share of the ξ_± diagonal variance within the
      fiducial cuts is 11% (see
      [mock_ptes_skew_low_by_ng_term](#../../findings.mock_ptes_skew_low_by_ng_term)).

      Across the 350 data-matched `baseline` realizations against the
      data covariances, the mean χ² exceeds ν for all five
      configuration-space statistics — 6.42 against ν = 6 for B_{n≤6},
      21.16 against 20 for B_{n≤20}, 8.33 against 7 for ξ_+^B, 7.32
      against 7 for ξ_-^B, 15.73 against 14 for ξ_tot^B — and sits
      slightly below for C_ℓ^BB, 16.40 against 17 (`published`: 6.84,
      22.12, 8.64, 7.73, 16.04, 16.47). A mean χ² above ν makes the
      reported PTEs lower than the true tail probabilities.
    created_at: "2026-08-29T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: mock_campaign_evidence
        quote:
          exact: '"chi2_mean": 6.418132939084542'
      - id: ev2
        artifact: mock_campaign_evidence
        quote:
          exact: '"chi2_mean": 16.396916247026443'
    scope: "350 data-matched GLASS realizations at fiducial scale cuts against data covariances (`baseline`)."

  tests_are_not_redundant:
    id: tests_are_not_redundant
    label: "Null-test statistics are not redundant"
    claim: |
      The six B-mode test statistics are not perfectly correlated
      across the clean realizations: statistics from different
      estimator families correlate only moderately, and even pairs
      sharing a data vector stay well below unity. This is why the
      minimum PTE over the six skews low and its threshold is
      calibrated on the mocks
      ([pte_threshold](#../../analyses.significance.decisions.pte_threshold)).
    notes: |
      χ² Pearson correlations across the 350 data-matched `baseline`
      realizations (`correlations.chi2.pearson_matrix` in
      `mock_campaign_evidence`). Different families, 0.21–0.42: 0.37
      B_{n≤6}–ξ_+^B, 0.28 B_{n≤6}–C_ℓ^BB, 0.27 ξ_+^B–C_ℓ^BB, 0.35
      ξ_-^B–C_ℓ^BB, 0.41 ξ_tot^B–C_ℓ^BB. Shared data vector: 0.74
      ξ_+^B–ξ_tot^B and 0.64 ξ_-^B–ξ_tot^B (nested by construction),
      0.53 B_{n≤6}–B_{n≤20}. The PTE Pearson matrix tells the same
      story (0.29 for B_{n≤6} with C_ℓ^BB).
    created_at: "2026-08-29T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        artifact: mock_campaign_evidence
        quote:
          exact: "0.7377686873430731"
    scope: "350 data-matched GLASS realizations (`baseline`), fiducial scale cuts, six-statistic χ² and PTE stacks."
