texts.analyses/covariances/astra.yaml:
version: "0.0.14"
name: "Covariances"
description: |
  Every covariance of the analysis: `CosmoCov` ξ_± covariances on the
  integration and reporting grids, NaMaster iNKA covariances of the Cℓ
  bandpowers, and the pure E/B and COSEBI covariances, which carry the ξ_±
  covariance through the linear transforms of the data vectors as M C_ξ Mᵀ and
  Tᵀ C_ξ T. Those two read the bin centres and pair counts of the
  [ξ_± measurement](#inputs.xi_integration) and none of its shear. The
  [reference covariances](#decisions.reference_covariance) are the same recipes
  at the noise the GLASS mocks are held against, kept apart from the data
  covariances the null tests read, and a [scan](#outputs.blind_cov_sweep) repeats
  them across the n(z) blinds.

inputs:
  # Count maps and shape-noise sums: the window and noise of the Cℓ covariances.
  - id: catalog_summary
    from: ../catalog_processing.catalog_summary

  # Realization 00001's summary: the window and noise of the mock-matched Cℓ covariance.
  - id: glass_mock_realization_00001
    from: ../mocks.glass_mock_realization_00001

  - id: redshift_distributions
    from: ../redshift_distributions
    # The theory of the CosmoCov and iNKA covariances, for every catalog version.

  # Each catalog's survey area, the area of every CosmoCov covariance.
  - id: survey_areas
    from: ../survey_areas

  # Pair counts and bin centres for the transforms; the shear columns are not read.
  - id: xi_reporting
    from: ../catalog_processing.xi_reporting

  - id: xi_integration
    from: ../catalog_processing.xi_integration

  - id: xi_sweep
    from: ../catalog_processing.xi_sweep

outputs:
  - id: cosmology_snapshot
    type: data
    description: |
      The Planck 2018 fiducial cosmology
      (`sp_validation.cosmology.PLANCK18`) as JSON: Ω_m = 0.30966,
      Ω_b = 0.04897, h = 0.6766, n_s = 0.9665, σ_8 = 0.8102, in flat
      ΛCDM with Ω_v = 1 − Ω_m. It sets the cosmology of every
      CosmoCov run.
    format: json
    decisions: [fiducial_cosmology]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python -c "import json; from sp_validation.cosmology import PLANCK18; d = dict(PLANCK18); d['Omega_v'] = 1 - PLANCK18['Omega_m']; json.dump(d, open('{output}', 'w'), indent=2)"

  - id: cov_reporting_g
    type: data
    description: |
      Reporting-grid 20-bin Gaussian-only CosmoCov covariance for
      the [fiducial catalog](#decisions.fiducial_catalog) at
      [blind A](#decisions.fiducial_blind), with area-only geometry:
      the Gaussian part of the [Gaussian + non-Gaussian diagnostic](#outputs.cov_reporting_ng).
      Together they give the non-Gaussian share of the ξ_±
      diagonal variance quoted in the paper.
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, covariance_engine, reporting_binning, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [cosmology_snapshot, redshift_distributions, survey_areas]
    format: txt
    recipe:
      command: >
        bash src/workflow/scripts/run_cosmocov_chain.sh
        --version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})" --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind}
        --min-sep 1.0 --max-sep 250.0 --nbins 20 --gaussian g
        --planck18-json {inputs.cosmology_snapshot}
        --nz "$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py nz_file {decisions.fiducial_blind})"
        --emit processed_g --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 4, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: cov_reporting_ng
    type: data
    description: |
      Reporting-grid 20-bin full Gaussian + non-Gaussian
      CosmoCov covariance for the
      [fiducial catalog](#decisions.fiducial_catalog) at
      [blind A](#decisions.fiducial_blind), including
      connected-trispectrum and super-sample-covariance terms. The
      super-sample term uses CosmoCov's circular window of the survey
      area, and the Gaussian part the area alone.
      It sets the non-Gaussian share of the diagonal variance
      quoted in the paper and the total-ξ_± error bars of the
      [pure-mode data-vector figure](#../analyses.significance.outputs.pure_eb_data_vector_figure),
      but does not enter the PTEs, which use
      the [selected integration covariance](#decisions.covariance_class).
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, covariance_engine, reporting_binning, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [cosmology_snapshot, redshift_distributions, survey_areas]
    format: txt
    recipe:
      command: >
        bash src/workflow/scripts/run_cosmocov_chain.sh
        --version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})" --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind}
        --min-sep 1.0 --max-sep 250.0 --nbins 20 --gaussian ng
        --planck18-json {inputs.cosmology_snapshot}
        --nz "$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py nz_file {decisions.fiducial_blind})"
        --emit processed --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 4, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: cov_integration
    type: data
    description: |
      Integration-grid 1000-bin CosmoCov covariance for the
      [fiducial catalog](#decisions.fiducial_catalog) at
      [blind A](#decisions.fiducial_blind), on 0.5–300 arcmin.
      The [covariance class](#decisions.covariance_class) is Gaussian-only
      on this grid, with area-only geometry.
      COSEBI covariances derive from it by a linear transform;
      pure-mode covariances use a linear transform or
      Monte Carlo draws, per the
      [construction](#decisions.pure_eb_covariance_method).
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, covariance_class, covariance_engine, integration_grid, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [cosmology_snapshot, redshift_distributions, survey_areas]
    format: txt
    recipe:
      command: >
        bash src/workflow/scripts/run_cosmocov_chain.sh
        --version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})" --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind}
        --min-sep 0.5 --max-sep 300.0 --nbins 1000
        --gaussian {decisions.covariance_class}
        --planck18-json {inputs.cosmology_snapshot}
        --nz "$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py nz_file {decisions.fiducial_blind})"
        --emit processed --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 4, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: cov_integration_reference
    type: data
    description: |
      [cov_integration](#outputs.cov_integration) at the noise the
      [reference covariance](#decisions.reference_covariance) selects: the
      covariance the GLASS mocks are held against, and the ξ_± half of the
      reference (the pure-E/B half is
      [pure_eb_covariance_reference](#outputs.pure_eb_covariance_reference)).
      Under `mockmatched` that is `source_n_gal = 5.79308 arcmin⁻²` and
      `sigma_e = 0.37926` (0.26817 per component) at the fiducial
      `area = 2894.0304 deg²`; under `data_covariance` it is
      [cov_integration](#outputs.cov_integration) itself.

      Under `mockmatched`, with the area held fixed, that n_gal
      corresponds to 60.36 M galaxies, 0.1% below the 60 423 575 of
      v1.4.6.3_v2 realization 00001, which raises the noise variance by
      0.2%. See
      [mocks_are_over_constraining](#../analyses.validation.analyses.glass_mocks.findings.mocks_are_over_constraining).
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, reference_covariance, mock_suite, covariance_class, covariance_engine, integration_grid, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [cov_integration, cosmology_snapshot, redshift_distributions, survey_areas]
    format: txt
    recipe:
      command: |
        if [ {decisions.reference_covariance} = data_covariance ]; then
          cp {inputs.cov_integration} {output}
        else
          bash src/workflow/scripts/run_cosmocov_chain.sh \
            --version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})" --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind} \
            --min-sep 0.5 --max-sep 300.0 --nbins 1000 \
            --gaussian {decisions.covariance_class} \
            --reference-covariance {decisions.reference_covariance} \
            --planck18-json {inputs.cosmology_snapshot} \
            --nz "$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py nz_file {decisions.fiducial_blind})" \
            --emit processed --out-file {output}
        fi
      resources: { cpus: 4, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: cov_reporting_reference
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      [cov_integration_reference](#outputs.cov_integration_reference)
      rebinned from the 1000-bin integration grid to the 20 reporting
      bins, `Cov_rep = B Cov_fine Bᵀ`, the reference for raw ξ_±. `B`
      weights each fine bin by a uniform field's pair density
      (θ_r² − θ_l²), approximating TreeCorr's pair-weighted binning; the
      unweighted `pointwise` operator of the `adaptive_dqags` chain
      is written alongside as `cov_pointwise`, and the two σ agree to
      1.3% at worst.
    decisions: [reference_covariance, mock_suite, integration_grid, reporting_binning]
    inputs: [cov_integration_reference]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/xi_reporting_covariance.py
        --covariance {inputs.cov_integration_reference}
        --reporting-binning {decisions.reporting_binning}
        --integration-grid {decisions.integration_grid}
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 2, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: cl_cov_reporting
    type: data
    description: |
      Gaussian (NaMaster iNKA) covariance of the Cℓ
      bandpowers for the fiducial catalog at blind A, on the
      32-bandpower √ℓ-spaced grid of
      [the harmonic-space data vector](#../analyses.catalog_processing.outputs.cl_bandpowers_reporting), the prescription
      Paper IV uses for its BB and EB null tests. It takes a Planck
      2018 theory spectrum plus analytic noise, with the weighted
      galaxy-count map at nside 1024 as the window.
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, bandpower_binning, noise_bias_correction, leakage_correction, fiducial_cosmology]
    inputs: [catalog_summary, redshift_distributions]
    format: fits
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/generate_cl_cov.py
        --ver "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})"
        --summary {inputs.catalog_summary} --cat-config src/cosmo_val/cat_config.yaml
        --nside 1024 --binning powspace --nbins 32 --power 0.5 --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind}
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 12, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: cl_cov_fine
    type: data
    description: |
      As [cl_cov_reporting](#outputs.cl_cov_reporting), on the
      √ℓ-spaced fine grid (96 bandpowers in the fiducial analysis) of
      [cl_bandpowers_fine](#../analyses.catalog_processing.outputs.cl_bandpowers_fine),
      for the harmonic-space COSEBI transform. The other three
      leak-corrected catalogs' counterparts come from the
      [cl_cov_scan sweep](#outputs.cl_cov_sweep).
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, harmonic_validation_binning, noise_bias_correction, leakage_correction, fiducial_cosmology]

    format: fits
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/generate_cl_cov.py
        --ver "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})"
        --summary {inputs.catalog_summary} --cat-config src/cosmo_val/cat_config.yaml
        --nside 1024 --binning powspace --nbins "$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py harmonic_validation_binning {decisions.harmonic_validation_binning})" --power 0.5 --blind {decisions.fiducial_blind}
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 12, memory: "32GB" }

  - id: cl_cov_reference
    type: data
    description: |
      [cl_cov_reporting](#outputs.cl_cov_reporting) on the catalog the
      [reference covariance](#decisions.reference_covariance) selects:
      realization 00001 of the [GLASS suite](#decisions.mock_suite) under
      `mockmatched`, and cl_cov_reporting itself under `data_covariance`.
      The method is catalog-driven (mask = the weighted galaxy-count map,
      noise bias Ω_pix ⟨Σ_i w_i² σ_{e,i}²⟩, both from the catalog's
      summary), so the option names a catalog and no number density or
      area convention enters. For the v1.4.6.3_v2
      suite under `mockmatched`, the mock's variance ratio to the data is
      0.725 over 300 ≤ ℓ ≤ 1600, against the 350 realizations' empirical
      0.716
      ([clbb_variance_ratios](#../analyses.validation.analyses.glass_mocks.outputs.clbb_variance_ratios)).
    decisions: [fiducial_blind, reference_covariance, mock_suite, bandpower_binning, noise_bias_correction, fiducial_cosmology]
    inputs: [cl_cov_reporting, glass_mock_realization_00001, redshift_distributions]
    format: fits
    recipe:
      command: |
        if [ {decisions.reference_covariance} = data_covariance ]; then
          cp {inputs.cl_cov_reporting} {output}
        else
          python src/workflow/scripts/generate_cl_cov.py \
            --ver SP_v1.4.6.3_glass_mock_v2 --summary {inputs.glass_mock_realization_00001} \

  - id: cov_sweep
    # Integration-grid covariances of the other catalog variants.

  - id: cl_cov_sweep

    # [cosebis_harmonic_scan](#../analyses.validation.analyses.cosebis_harmonic_scan.outputs.cosebis_harmonic_version_ptes).
    from: cl_cov_scan.cl_cov_sweep_bundle

  - id: pure_eb_covariance
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      The 120×120 covariance (six 20-bin blocks) of the pure E/B data vector
      [pure_eb_data](#../analyses.catalog_processing.outputs.pure_eb_data) for the
      [fiducial catalog](#../decisions.fiducial_catalog) at blind A, propagated
      from [cov_integration](#outputs.cov_integration) by the selected
      [covariance method](#decisions.pure_eb_covariance_method). The file
      records that construction (and the draw count, for the Monte Carlo) so χ²
      consumers apply the matching Hartlap treatment. The transform M weights
      fine bins by the [measured pair counts](#inputs.xi_integration); the
      Monte Carlo draws of ξ_± produce this covariance and nothing else.
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, pure_eb_integration_method, pure_eb_rebinning_weights, pure_eb_integration_limits, pure_eb_covariance_method, decomposition_method, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [xi_reporting, xi_integration, cov_integration, redshift_distributions]

        --xi-reporting {inputs.xi_reporting}
        --xi-integration {inputs.xi_integration}
        --cov-integration {inputs.cov_integration}
        --integration-method {decisions.pure_eb_integration_method}
        --integration-limits {decisions.pure_eb_integration_limits}
        --rebinning-weights {decisions.pure_eb_rebinning_weights}

      [reference ξ_± covariance](#outputs.cov_integration_reference): the
      same transform M, built from the data's pair counts, or the same Monte
      Carlo chain with the same draws, so the two differ by their input
      alone. The reference noise enters only through that covariance, as
      it does for COSEBIs; under `data_covariance` this is
      pure_eb_covariance itself.
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, reference_covariance, mock_suite, pure_eb_integration_method, pure_eb_rebinning_weights, pure_eb_integration_limits, pure_eb_covariance_method, decomposition_method, leakage_correction, integration_grid]
    inputs: [pure_eb_covariance, xi_reporting, xi_integration, cov_integration_reference, redshift_distributions]
    recipe:
      command: |
        if [ {decisions.reference_covariance} = data_covariance ]; then
          cp {inputs.pure_eb_covariance} {output}
        else
          bash src/papers/bmodes/scripts/run_pure_eb_covariance.sh \
            --version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})" --blind "$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py fiducial_blind {decisions.fiducial_blind})" \
            --cat-config src/cosmo_val/cat_config.yaml \
            --xi-reporting {inputs.xi_reporting} \
            --xi-integration {inputs.xi_integration} \
            --cov-integration {inputs.cov_integration_reference} \
            --integration-method {decisions.pure_eb_integration_method} \
            --integration-limits {decisions.pure_eb_integration_limits} \
            --rebinning-weights {decisions.pure_eb_rebinning_weights} \
            --covariance-method {decisions.pure_eb_covariance_method} \
            --out-file {output}
        fi
      resources: { cpus: 24, memory: "60GB" }

  - id: pure_eb_covariance_sweep
    type: data
    format: tar.gz
    description: |
      [pure_eb_covariance](#outputs.pure_eb_covariance) for the seven
      non-fiducial catalog versions (the other three variants with and without
      the leakage correction, and the fiducial variant with the opposite
      treatment), one npz each, from that version's ξ_±
      ([xi_sweep](#inputs.xi_sweep)) and Gaussian integration covariance
      ([cov_sweep](#outputs.cov_sweep)).
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, pure_eb_integration_method, pure_eb_rebinning_weights, pure_eb_integration_limits, pure_eb_covariance_method, decomposition_method, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [xi_sweep, cov_sweep, redshift_distributions]
    recipe:
      command: |
        set -e
        x=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.xi_sweep} -C $x
        c=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.cov_sweep} -C $c
        o=$(mktemp -d)
        b="$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py fiducial_blind {decisions.fiducial_blind})"
        versions=$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction} --nonfiducial)
        for ver in $versions; do
          cb=covariance_"$ver"_"$b"_integration
          bash src/papers/bmodes/scripts/run_pure_eb_covariance.sh \
            --version "$ver" --blind "$b" \
            --cat-config src/cosmo_val/cat_config.yaml \
            --xi-reporting "$x/$ver"_xi_minsep=1.0_maxsep=250.0_nbins=20_npatch=1.txt \
            --xi-integration "$x/$ver"_xi_minsep=0.5_maxsep=300.0_nbins=1000_npatch=1.txt \
            --cov-integration "$c/$cb/$cb"_processed.txt \
            --integration-method {decisions.pure_eb_integration_method} \
            --integration-limits {decisions.pure_eb_integration_limits} \
            --rebinning-weights {decisions.pure_eb_rebinning_weights} \
            --covariance-method {decisions.pure_eb_covariance_method} \
            --out-file "$o/$ver"_"$b"_pure_eb_covariance.npz
        done
        tar czf {output} -C $o .
      resources: { cpus: 16, memory: "60GB" }

  - id: cosebis_covariance
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      The COSEBI mode covariance T^T C_ξ T of
      [cosebis_modes_data](#../analyses.catalog_processing.outputs.cosebis_modes_data)
      at both scale cuts, from [cov_integration](#outputs.cov_integration), with
      the σ_n that normalise B_n / σ_n in the
      [COSEBI data-vector figure](#../outputs.fig_cosebis_fiducial). T depends on
      the [integration-grid bin centres](#inputs.xi_integration) inside each cut.
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, mode_count, leakage_correction, reporting_binning, integration_grid]
    inputs: [xi_integration, cov_integration]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/cosebis_covariance.py
        --version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})"
        --reporting-binning {decisions.reporting_binning} --integration-grid {decisions.integration_grid} --mode-count {decisions.mode_count}
        --xi-integration {inputs.xi_integration}
        --cov-integration {inputs.cov_integration}
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 8, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: cosebis_covariance_sweep
    type: data
    format: tar.gz
    description: |
      [cosebis_covariance](#outputs.cosebis_covariance) for the three other
      catalog versions of the
      [COSEBI version comparison](#../outputs.fig_versions_cosebis), one npz each,
      from that version's ξ_± ([xi_sweep](#inputs.xi_sweep)) and Gaussian
      integration covariance ([cov_sweep](#outputs.cov_sweep)).
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, fiducial_blind, mode_count, leakage_correction, reporting_binning, integration_grid]
    inputs: [xi_sweep, cov_sweep]
    recipe:
      command: |
        set -e
        x=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.xi_sweep} -C $x
        c=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.cov_sweep} -C $c
        o=$(mktemp -d)
        b="$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py fiducial_blind {decisions.fiducial_blind})"
        versions=$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction} --comparison)
        for ver in $versions; do
          cb=covariance_"$ver"_"$b"_integration
          python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/cosebis_covariance.py \
            --version "$ver" \
            --reporting-binning {decisions.reporting_binning} --integration-grid {decisions.integration_grid} --mode-count {decisions.mode_count} \
            --xi-integration "$x/$ver"_xi_minsep=0.5_maxsep=300.0_nbins=1000_npatch=1.txt \
            --cov-integration "$c/$cb/$cb"_processed.txt \
            --out-file "$o/$ver"_"$b"_cosebis_covariance.npz
        done
        tar czf {output} -C $o .
      resources: { cpus: 8, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: blind_cov_sweep
    # The ξ_±, pure E/B and Cℓ covariances at each n(z) blind, for the
    # [blind-independence check](#../analyses.validation.outputs.bb_covariance_blind_independence_evidence).
    from: blind_cov_scan.blind_cov_sweep_bundle

  - id: pure_eb_covariance_figure
    type: figure
    description: |
      Correlation matrix of the pure E/B covariance for the [fiducial
      catalog](#decisions.fiducial_catalog), propagated from the
      CosmoCov ξ_± covariance, in six 20-bin blocks: ξ_+^E,
      ξ_-^E, ξ_+^B, ξ_-^B, ξ_+^amb, ξ_-^amb. Off-diagonal correlations
      arise from integral coupling in the pure-mode filters.
    format: png
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [pure_eb_covariance]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/pure_eb_covariance.py
        --fiducial-catalog {decisions.fiducial_catalog} --leakage-correction {decisions.leakage_correction}
        --pure-eb-covariance {inputs.pure_eb_covariance}
        --out-file {output}


decisions:
  integration_grid:
    from: ../integration_grid
  reporting_binning:
    from: ../reporting_binning
  noise_bias_correction:
    from: ../noise_bias_correction
  bandpower_binning:
    from: ../bandpower_binning
  fiducial_cosmology:
    label: "Fiducial cosmology for covariance theory"
    tags: [covariance_model]
    rationale: |
      The analytic covariance needs a fixed cosmology for
      its matter power spectrum. Planck 2018 + BAO ΛCDM is the
      community reference and is shared with the covariances of
      Papers III and IV. No alternative is exposed: the B modes are
      tested against zero, so the cosmology enters only through the
      covariance.
    default: planck18
    options:
      planck18:
        label: "Planck 2018 + BAO"
        description: |
          Ω_m=0.30966, σ_8=0.8102, n_s=0.9665, Ω_b=0.04897,
          h=0.6766 (astropy `Planck18`).
        insights: [planck18_fiducial_cosmology]
  leakage_correction:
    from: ../leakage_correction

  fiducial_catalog:
    from: ../fiducial_catalog

  fiducial_blind:
    from: ../fiducial_blind

  harmonic_validation_binning:
    from: ../harmonic_validation_binning

  pure_eb_integration_method:
    from: ../pure_eb_integration_method

  pure_eb_rebinning_weights:
    from: ../pure_eb_rebinning_weights

  pure_eb_integration_limits:
    from: ../pure_eb_integration_limits

  pure_eb_covariance_method:
    label: "Pure-mode covariance construction"
    tags: [covariance_model]
    rationale: |
      The [fixed-quadrature estimator](#../decisions.pure_eb_integration_method)
      is exactly linear in the fine ξ_± vector, ξ^{E/B/amb} =
      M · [ξ_+; ξ_−], so its covariance is M C_ξ Mᵀ with C_ξ the
      CosmoCov covariance. The two options are two ways of
      evaluating that matrix. The Monte Carlo pushes Gaussian draws
      of ξ_± through the transform and applies the Hartlap factor at
      χ² time; it equals M Ĉ_ξ Mᵀ with Ĉ_ξ the draws' sample
      covariance, so it differs from the exact matrix only by
      sampling noise.

      The exact matrix is adopted. It is noise-free, so no Hartlap
      factor enters, and it removes a noise term from every
      pure-mode PTE and from the mock-calibrated threshold built
      under the same covariance. It requires a linear operator, so
      `adaptive_dqags` can only use the Monte Carlo.
    default: exact_linear
    options:
      exact_linear:
        label: "Exact M C_ξ Mᵀ"
        description: |
          M from the averaged transform applied to the 2000 fine-grid
          unit vectors; C_ξ is the CosmoCov covariance (data) or its
          reference twin. No Hartlap factor. Under it the
          data-to-mock-matched B variance ratio of the v1.4.6.3_v2 suite
          is a constant 1.353
          across ξ^B bins, as expected for a shape-noise B-mode
          covariance.
      monte_carlo:
        label: "Monte Carlo, Hartlap-corrected"
        description: |
          Sample covariance of 2000 draws
          from C_ξ through the same transform, with the Hartlap
          factor (N − p − 2)/(N − 1) on its inverse; the only option
          available to `adaptive_dqags`. It reproduces M Ĉ_ξ Mᵀ to
          1e-15, and its differences from the exact matrix all lie
          within 1.5σ of the simulated MC scatter (fiducial ξ_−^B PTE
          0.025 against 0.019, MC scatter 0.004). Its per-bin
          data-to-mock-matched B variance ratio of that suite spreads over
          1.23–1.43, which is noise.
        insights: [hartlap07_correction]

  decomposition_method:
    from: ../decomposition_method

  mode_count:
    from: ../mode_count

  reference_covariance:
    from: ../reference_covariance

  mock_suite:
    from: ../mock_suite

  covariance_engine:
    label: "Covariance engine"
    tags: [covariance_model]
    rationale: |
      `CosmoCov` (Krause & Eifler 2017; Fang, Eifler & Krause 2020)
      computes every ξ_± covariance in this analysis.
      Each B-mode statistic starts from the covariance
      prescription of its companion cosmology paper. For ξ_±
      (and the pure-mode and COSEBI statistics derived from it)
      that is `CosmoCov`, Paper III's analytic code, whose 2D-FFTLog
      transforms give numerically stable real-space covariances
      without simulations. For Cℓ^BB and Cℓ^EB it is NaMaster's
      iNKA Gaussian covariance, as in Paper IV's B-mode null
      tests. The GLASS mocks validate both rather than replace
      them. CosmoCov computes the shear-shear covariance as three
      blocks, ++ (ξ_+ auto), -- (ξ_- auto) and +- (cross), all
      required: the joint ξ_tot^B test needs the cross-block, and
      the pure-mode and COSEBI transforms mix ξ_+ and ξ_-.
    default: cosmocov
    options:
      cosmocov:
        label: "CosmoCov (configuration-space)"
        insights: [fang20_2dfftlog_stable_real_space_covariance]
        description: |
          Analytic configuration-space covariance code of Krause
          & Eifler 2017 and Fang, Eifler & Krause 2020. It computes
          the ξ_± covariances on the
          [integration](#outputs.cov_integration) and
          [reporting](#outputs.cov_reporting_ng) grids and for the
          [catalog versions](#outputs.cov_sweep), each through
          `run_cosmocov_chain.sh`.
      namaster_inka:
        label: "NaMaster iNKA (harmonic-space)"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "iNKA supplies the harmonic covariance, not an alternative implementation of the configuration-space CosmoCov covariance."
        description: |
          NaMaster's improved Narrow Kernel Approximation
          Gaussian bandpower covariance, which Paper IV validates
          against Gaussian simulations (their Appendix C).
      mock_sample_covariance:
        label: "GLASS sample covariance"
        description: |
          Sample covariance across the 350 GLASS mock
          realizations.
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: |
          The PTEs follow the analytic prescriptions of Papers III
          and IV, which the mocks validate rather than replace. A
          350-realization sample covariance would also be noisy, and
          singular on the 1000-bin integration grid.

  covariance_class:
    label: "Gaussian vs Gaussian + non-Gaussian covariance"
    tags: [covariance_model]
    rationale: |
      The fiducial B-mode null tests use only the Gaussian part of the
      covariance. In configuration space this keeps the
      calculation tractable on the fine integration grid;
      in harmonic space Paper IV likewise adds non-Gaussian
      terms only for its EE cosmology analysis. Omitting the
      connected-trispectrum and super-sample terms
      underestimates the variances by a
      [modest share](#../findings.mock_ptes_skew_low_by_ng_term), so
      the null tests are
      conservative: a test that passes with the Gaussian-only
      covariance would generally pass with a more complete one,
      as the GLASS mocks confirm.
      The non-Gaussian contribution is quantified only on the reporting grid.
    default: gaussian_only
    options:
      gaussian_only:
        label: "Gaussian only"
        description: |
          Gaussian CosmoCov terms on both grids; NaMaster iNKA
          is Gaussian by construction.
      gaussian_plus_ng:
        label: "Gaussian + non-Gaussian"
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Non-Gaussian terms are intractable on the 1000-bin integration grid; their size is quantified on the reporting grid by cov_reporting_ng."
        description: |
          CosmoCov's connected-trispectrum and super-sample terms,
          evaluated in the fixed 20-bin diagnostic only.
          The harmonic-space iNKA covariance remains Gaussian.

analyses:

  cov_scan:
    path: ./analyses/cov_scan

  cl_cov_scan:
    path: ./analyses/cl_cov_scan

  blind_cov_scan:
    path: ./analyses/blind_cov_scan

prior_insights:

  fang20_2dfftlog_stable_real_space_covariance:
    id: fang20_2dfftlog_stable_real_space_covariance
    claim: |
      Analytic covariances are much faster and less noisy than
      estimates from data or simulations; the 2D-FFTLog algorithm
      released with CosmoCov makes the Bessel-integral transform to
      real space numerically stable and produces angular
      bin-averaged covariances accurate enough for cosmological
      inference.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1093/mnras/staa1726"
        quote:
          exact: "Among various approaches to obtaining the covariance, analytic computation is much faster and less noisy than estimation from data or simulations."
        location:
          page: 1
      - id: ev2
        doi: "10.1093/mnras/staa1726"
        quote:
          exact: "our algorithm can produce numerically stable angular bin-averaged covariances with the flat sky approximation, which are sufficiently accurate for inferring cosmological parameters."
        location:
          page: 1
    scope: |
      Fang, Eifler & Krause 2020, MNRAS 497, 2699; validated for
      DES-Y3- and LSST-Y1-like surveys.

  hartlap07_correction:
    id: hartlap07_correction
    claim: |
      For an inverse covariance estimated from N independent
      Gaussian samples on a data vector of length p, the
      maximum-likelihood inverse is biased; the unbiased
      estimator multiplies it by (N - p - 2) / (N - 1). For
      analytic (theory) covariances the correction does
      not apply because no sample uncertainty enters.
    created_at: "2026-04-25T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361:20066170"
        quote:
          exact: |
            We find that the inverse of the maximum-likelihood
            estimator of the covariance is biased, the amount of
            bias depending on the ratio of the number of bins
            (data vector variables), p, to the number of data
            sets, n. This bias inevitably leads to an -- in
            extreme cases catastrophic -- underestimation of
            the size of the confidence regions.
          prefix: "Methods. We perform Monte-Carlo simulations to investigate the behaviour of estimators for the inverse covariance matrix"
          suffix: "We report on a method to remove this bias for the idealised case of Gaussian errors and statistically independent data vectors."
        location:
          page: 1
    scope: "Sample covariances of Gaussian data, not theory covariances (Hartlap et al. 2007, Eq. 17)."

  planck18_fiducial_cosmology:
    id: planck18_fiducial_cosmology
    claim: |
      The Planck 2018 baseline ΛCDM cosmology (Ω_m = 0.315 ± 0.007,
      σ_8 = 0.811 ± 0.006, H_0 = 67.4 ± 0.5 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹,
      Ω_b h² = 0.0224 ± 0.0001, n_s = 0.965 ± 0.004) is the community
      reference for late-Universe parameters.
    created_at: "2026-04-25T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/201833910"
        quote:
          exact: |
            Assuming the base-ΛCDM cosmology, the inferred
            (model-dependent) late-Universe parameters are:
            Hubble constant H_0 = (67.4 ± 0.5) km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹;
            matter density parameter Ω_m = 0.315 ± 0.007; and
            matter fluctuation amplitude σ_8 = 0.811 ± 0.006.
          prefix: "These results are only weakly dependent on the cosmological model and remain stable, with somewhat increased errors, in many commonly considered extensions."
          suffix: "We find no compelling evidence for extensions to the base-ΛCDM model."
        location:
          page: 1
    scope: "Base ΛCDM (Planck Collaboration VI 2020, A&A 641, A6)"
    notes: |
      The covariance uses the Planck 2018 + BAO parameters of astropy
      `Planck18` (Ω_m = 0.30966, σ_8 = 0.8102, h = 0.6766), which sit
      within 1.7% of these central values.

  Gaussian CosmoCov covariance for all three ξ± pairings, carried exactly

# ============================================================
# GENERATED by astra-sweep from blind_cov_scan.sweep.yaml -- DO NOT EDIT
#
# 3 member outputs + 1 gather output.

id: blind_cov_scan
version: '1.0'
name: Covariance scan over the n(z) blinds
description: |

  [fiducial catalog](#../decisions.fiducial_catalog): the
  Gaussian CosmoCov ξ_± covariance on the integration grid, its propagation
  through the pure-mode transform, and the iNKA covariance of the 32 bandpowers,
  each by the recipe of its fiducial counterpart. Only the n(z) moves between
  members. The gathered result feeds the
  [blind-independence check](#../../../analyses.validation.outputs.bb_covariance_blind_independence_evidence).
tags:
- sweep
inputs:
- id: cosmology_snapshot
  from: ../../covariances.cosmology_snapshot
- id: redshift_distributions
  from: ../redshift_distributions
- id: survey_areas
  from: ../survey_areas

- id: xi_integration

  decomposition_method:

    [cov_integration](#../outputs.cov_integration),
    [pure_eb_covariance](#../outputs.pure_eb_covariance) and
    [cl_cov_reporting](#../outputs.cl_cov_reporting) with that blind's n(z).

  - redshift_distributions

  - catalog_summary
  - xi_reporting
  - xi_integration

  - leakage_correction
  - covariance_class
  - covariance_engine
  - integration_grid

  - noise_bias_correction

  - pure_eb_rebinning_weights
  - pure_eb_integration_limits
  - pure_eb_covariance_method
  - decomposition_method
  recipe:
    command: |
      set -e
      version=$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})
      o=$(mktemp -d)
      bash src/workflow/scripts/run_cosmocov_chain.sh \
        --version "$version" --blind blind_a \
        --min-sep 0.5 --max-sep 300.0 --nbins 1000 \
        --gaussian {decisions.covariance_class} \
        --planck18-json {inputs.cosmology_snapshot} \
        --emit processed --out-file "$o"/cov_integration_blind_a.txt
      bash src/papers/bmodes/scripts/run_pure_eb_covariance.sh \
        --version "$version" --blind "$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py fiducial_blind blind_a)" \
        --cat-config src/cosmo_val/cat_config.yaml \
        --xi-reporting {inputs.xi_reporting} \
        --xi-integration {inputs.xi_integration} \
        --cov-integration "$o"/cov_integration_blind_a.txt \
        --integration-method {decisions.pure_eb_integration_method} \
        --integration-limits {decisions.pure_eb_integration_limits} \
        --rebinning-weights {decisions.pure_eb_rebinning_weights} \
        --covariance-method {decisions.pure_eb_covariance_method} \
        --out-file "$o"/pure_eb_covariance_blind_a.npz
      python src/workflow/scripts/generate_cl_cov.py \
        --ver "$version" --summary {inputs.catalog_summary} \
        --cat-config src/cosmo_val/cat_config.yaml \
        --nside 1024 --binning powspace --nbins 32 --power 0.5 --blind blind_a \
        --out-file "$o"/cl_cov_blind_a.fits
      tar czf {output} -C $o .
    resources:
      cpus: 24
      memory: 60GB
  format: tar.gz
- id: blind_covariances_blind_b
  type: data
  description: |
    The ξ_±, pure E/B and Cℓ covariances at `blind_b`:
    [cov_integration](#../outputs.cov_integration),
    [pure_eb_covariance](#../outputs.pure_eb_covariance) and
    [cl_cov_reporting](#../outputs.cl_cov_reporting) with that blind's n(z).
  inputs:

  decisions:

      python src/workflow/scripts/generate_cl_cov.py \

- id: blind_covariances_blind_c
  type: data
  description: |
    The ξ_±, pure E/B and Cℓ covariances at `blind_c`:

texts.analyses/catalog_processing/astra.yaml:
version: "0.0.14"
name: "Catalog processing"
description: |
  Everything the analysis takes from the shear catalogs, and the only place
  that reads them. ξ_± and Cℓ are measured from the catalogs: TreeCorr ξ_±(θ)
  on a 20-bin reporting grid and a 1000-bin integration grid, with one
  10,000-bin run for the convergence check, and catalog-based Cℓ bandpowers on
  the 32-bandpower and fine grids. The [catalog summary](#outputs.catalog_summary)
  holds what the covariances and the GLASS mocks need from each catalog. Pure
  E/B modes and COSEBIs are linear transforms of ξ_±: the Schneider et al.
  (2022) decomposition into pure E, pure B and ambiguous modes, and the
  discrete E_n and B_n, whose filters are built for a given angular range. Each
  is computed for the fiducial catalog and across catalog versions.

inputs:
  - id: shapepipe_v14_catalogs
    from: ../shapepipe_v14_catalogs

outputs:
  - id: catalog_summary
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      What the covariances and the GLASS mocks take from each of the five
      catalogs: the weighted nside-1024 galaxy-count map, which is the window
      of the NaMaster Cℓ covariances; the nside-4096 pixels holding a galaxy,
      the footprint the GLASS realizations are sampled in; and the galaxy
      count, Σw, Σw² and Σw²(e₁² + e₂²)/2 on the raw and leakage-corrected
      ellipticities, from which follow the weight-effective count (Σw)²/Σw²
      and the per-component σ_e the shape noise of the covariances and the
      data-matched mocks is set by. The weight-effective counts reproduce
      Paper I's n_eff on its footprint areas, and the σ_e its dispersions.
      The occupied-pixel footprints cover 2750.65 deg² for the size-cut
      catalog, 2807.33, 2371.49 and 2790.96 deg² for the initial, masked and
      relaxed-flags ones, and 2757.25 deg² for v1.4.6.
    inputs: [shapepipe_v14_catalogs]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/catalog_summary.py
        --catalog SP_v1.4.5=data/v1.4.x/v1.4.5/unions_shapepipe_cut_struc_2024_v1.4.5.fits
        --catalog SP_v1.4.6=data/v1.4.x/v1.4.6/unions_shapepipe_cut_struc_2024_v1.4.6.fits
        --catalog SP_v1.4.6.3=data/v1.4.x/v1.4.6.3/unions_shapepipe_cut_struc_2024_v1.4.6.3.fits
        --catalog SP_v1.4.8=data/v1.4.x/v1.4.8/unions_shapepipe_cut_struc_2024_v1.4.8.fits
        --catalog SP_v1.4.11.3=data/v1.4.x/v1.4.11.3/unions_shapepipe_cut_struc_2024_v1.4.11.3.fits
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 4, memory: "64GB" }

  - id: xi_reporting
    type: data
    description: |
      TreeCorr ξ_±(θ) of the fiducial catalog on the reporting grid:
      20 logarithmic bins over [1', 250']. These are the bins the
      pure modes are reported in, and the total ξ_± shown beside
      them.
    format: txt
    inputs: [shapepipe_v14_catalogs]
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, reporting_binning, patch_count, leakage_correction]
    recipe:
      # --ver is the catalog version; its `_leak_corr` form reads the
      # leakage-corrected ellipticity columns of the same catalog.
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/run_2pcf.py
        --ver "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})" --min-sep 1.0 --max-sep 250.0 --nbins 20 --npatch 1
        --cat-config src/cosmo_val/cat_config.yaml
        --no-fits --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 24, memory: "30GB" }

  - id: xi_integration
    type: data
    description: |
      TreeCorr ξ_±(θ) of the fiducial catalog on the integration
      grid: 1000 logarithmic bins over [0.5', 300'], the input to
      the pure-mode and COSEBI integrals. The range extends beyond
      the reporting grid to reduce edge effects in the pure-mode
      boundary functions S_± and V_±.
    format: txt
    inputs: [shapepipe_v14_catalogs]
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, integration_grid, patch_count, leakage_correction]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/run_2pcf.py
        --ver "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})" --min-sep 0.5 --max-sep 300.0 --nbins 1000 --npatch 1
        --cat-config src/cosmo_val/cat_config.yaml
        --no-fits --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 24, memory: "30GB" }

  - id: xi_10000_bins
    type: data
    description: |
      TreeCorr ξ_±(θ) of the leakage-corrected size-cut catalog on a
      10,000-bin grid over [0.5', 300'], for the
      [convergence check](#../analyses.validation.outputs.integration_grid_convergence)
      of the 1000-bin integration grid. It is the expensive one, about 720
      core-hours on one node, because bins this fine blow up
      TreeCorr's pair traversal; no jackknife enters.
    format: txt
    when: [leakage_correction.applied]
    decisions: [leakage_correction]
    inputs: [shapepipe_v14_catalogs]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/run_2pcf_highres.py
        --cat-config src/cosmo_val/cat_config.yaml --version SP_v1.4.6.3_leak_corr
        --nbins 10000 --min-sep 0.5 --max-sep 300.0 --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 96, memory: "200GB" }

  - id: xi_sweep
    # The ξ_± of the catalog-version scan, read by the pure-mode and COSEBI
    # version comparisons.
    from: xi_scan.xi_sweep_bundle

  - id: pure_eb_data
    type: data
    description: |
      Pure E/B data vectors ξ_±^{E,B,amb} for the fiducial catalog on the
      20-bin reporting grid, with the total ξ_± beside them: the Schneider et
      al. (2022) transform of [xi_reporting](#outputs.xi_reporting) and
      [xi_integration](#outputs.xi_integration). Their covariance is
      [pure_eb_covariance](#../analyses.covariances.outputs.pure_eb_covariance).
    format: npz
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, pure_eb_integration_method, pure_eb_rebinning_weights, pure_eb_integration_limits, decomposition_method, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [xi_reporting, xi_integration]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/pure_eb_modes.py
        --xi-reporting {inputs.xi_reporting}
        --xi-integration {inputs.xi_integration}
        --integration-method {decisions.pure_eb_integration_method}
        --integration-limits {decisions.pure_eb_integration_limits}
        --rebinning-weights {decisions.pure_eb_rebinning_weights}
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 8, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: pure_eb_sweep
    type: data
    description: |
      Pure E/B data vectors for the seven non-fiducial catalog versions (the
      other three variants with and without the leakage correction, and the
      fiducial variant with the opposite treatment), one npz each, built as
      [pure_eb_data](#outputs.pure_eb_data) is from that version's ξ_±
      ([xi_sweep](#outputs.xi_sweep)).
    format: tar.gz
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, pure_eb_integration_method, pure_eb_rebinning_weights, pure_eb_integration_limits, decomposition_method, leakage_correction]
    inputs: [xi_sweep]
    recipe:
      command: |
        set -e
        x=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.xi_sweep} -C $x
        o=$(mktemp -d)
        versions=$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction} --nonfiducial)
        for ver in $versions; do
          python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/pure_eb_modes.py \
            --xi-reporting "$x/$ver"_xi_minsep=1.0_maxsep=250.0_nbins=20_npatch=1.txt \
            --xi-integration "$x/$ver"_xi_minsep=0.5_maxsep=300.0_nbins=1000_npatch=1.txt \
            --integration-method {decisions.pure_eb_integration_method} \
            --integration-limits {decisions.pure_eb_integration_limits} \
            --rebinning-weights {decisions.pure_eb_rebinning_weights} \
            --out-file "$o/$ver"_pure_eb_data.npz
        done
        tar czf {output} -C $o .
      resources: { cpus: 8, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: cosebis_modes_data
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      COSEBI E_n and B_n (n = 1 … 20) for the
      [fiducial catalog](#../decisions.fiducial_catalog) at both scale
      cuts, computed from [xi_integration](#outputs.xi_integration). Their
      covariance is
      [cosebis_covariance](#../analyses.covariances.outputs.cosebis_covariance).
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, mode_count, leakage_correction, reporting_binning, integration_grid]
    inputs: [xi_integration]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/cosebis_data_vector.py
        --version "$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction})"
        --reporting-binning {decisions.reporting_binning} --integration-grid {decisions.integration_grid} --mode-count {decisions.mode_count}
        --xi-integration {inputs.xi_integration}
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 8, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: cosebis_modes_sweep
    type: data
    format: tar.gz
    description: |
      [cosebis_modes_data](#outputs.cosebis_modes_data) for the three other
      catalog versions of the
      [COSEBI version comparison](#../outputs.fig_versions_cosebis), one npz
      each, from that version's ξ_± ([xi_sweep](#outputs.xi_sweep)).
    decisions: [fiducial_catalog, mode_count, leakage_correction, reporting_binning, integration_grid]
    inputs: [xi_sweep]
    recipe:
      command: |
        set -e
        x=$(mktemp -d) && tar xzf {inputs.xi_sweep} -C $x
        o=$(mktemp -d)
        versions=$(python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/catalog_versions.py {decisions.fiducial_catalog} {decisions.leakage_correction} --comparison)
        for ver in $versions; do
          python src/papers/bmodes/scripts/cosebis_data_vector.py \
            --version "$ver" \
            --reporting-binning {decisions.reporting_binning} --integration-grid {decisions.integration_grid} --mode-count {decisions.mode_count} \
            --xi-integration "$x/$ver"_xi_minsep=0.5_maxsep=300.0_nbins=1000_npatch=1.txt \
            --out-file "$o/$ver"_cosebis_modes.npz
        done

    from: ../noise_bias_correction
  patch_count:
    label: "TreeCorr patch decomposition"
    tags: [covariance_model]
    rationale: |
      For a ξ_± measurement, patches matter only through a
      jackknife covariance. The
      [ξ_± covariance](#../analyses.covariances.outputs.cov_integration) is
      analytic (CosmoCov), so the measurement runs on a single
      patch; a jackknife serves only as a development cross-check of
      the analytic covariance.
    default: npatch_1
    options:
      npatch_1:
        label: "1 patch"
        description: |
          Single-patch TreeCorr; no jackknife covariance.
      npatch_120:
        label: "120 patches"
        description: |
          Enables a spatial-jackknife covariance, which the paper
          reports agrees with the analytic ξ_± covariance at the
          ten-percent level over the fiducial range.
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: |
          The reported configuration-space PTEs use the CosmoCov
          covariance, not a jackknife.

  estimator_choice:
    label: "Cℓ estimator"
    tags: [estimator]
    rationale: |
      The Wolz et al. (2025) catalog-based estimator evaluates
      spin-2 spherical-harmonic transforms directly at source
      positions through the `ducc` library (Reinecke et al.
      2023), avoiding the pixelization artifacts of map-based
      pseudo-Cℓ. Paper IV measures its cosmic-shear spectra with
      the same estimator, so the null tests match the inference.
      Map-based pseudo-Cℓ, as used by DES and HSC, is the
      standard alternative.
    default: wolz25_catalog_based
    options:
      wolz25_catalog_based:
        label: "Wolz et al. 2025 catalog-based"
        description: |
          Spin-2 transforms at source positions via `ducc`, with
          NaMaster-decoupled bandpowers and analytic shot-noise
          subtraction.
        insights: [wolz25_catalog_based_pseudo_cl, hivon02_master_mode_coupling_deconvolution, alonso19_namaster_unbiased_spin2_pseudo_cl, reinecke23_sht_on_arbitrary_grids]
      map_based_pseudo_cl:
        excluded: true
        excluded_reason: "Not implemented here: the measurement recipes run only the catalog estimator, the GLASS mock spectra that validate it use the same one, and the iNKA covariance fails in the Monte-Carlo noise mode that matches the map estimator's noise subtraction."
        label: "Map-based pseudo-Cℓ on HEALPix"
        insights: [hivon02_master_mode_coupling_deconvolution, alonso19_namaster_unbiased_spin2_pseudo_cl]
        description: |
          Shapes binned into HEALPix pixels before the transform,
          which introduces pixel-window and aliasing effects near
          the pixel scale.

prior_insights:

  wolz25_catalog_based_pseudo_cl:
    id: wolz25_catalog_based_pseudo_cl
    claim: |
      The catalog-based pseudo-Cℓ estimator measures power
      spectra of fields sampled at arbitrary source positions,
      without pixelized maps; subtracting the discrete mask's
      shot noise analytically makes it immune to pixelization
      and aliasing and unbiased against noise uncorrelated
      between sources.
    created_at: "2026-04-25T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1088/1475-7516/2025/01/028"
        quote:
          exact: |
            We present a formalism to extract the angular
            power spectrum of fields sampled at a finite
            number of points with arbitrary positions -- a
            common situation for several catalog-based
            astrophysical probes -- through a simple extension
            of the standard pseudo-$C_\ell$ algorithm.
          prefix: "Abstract."
          suffix: "A key complication in this case is the need to handle the shot noise component of the associated discrete angular mask"
        location:
          page: 1
      - id: ev2
        doi: "10.1088/1475-7516/2025/01/028"
        quote:
          exact: |
            The resulting estimator is immune to small-scale
            pixelization effects and aliasing, and, more
            interestingly, unbiased against the contribution
            from measurement noise uncorrelated between
            different sources.
          prefix: "We show that this problem can be solved easily by estimating this contribution analytically and subtracting it."
          suffix: "We demonstrate the validity of the method in the context of cosmic shear datasets"
        location:
          page: 1
    scope: |
      Wolz, Alonso & Nicola 2025, JCAP 01, 028; the basis of the
      [harmonic-space](#outputs.cl_bandpowers_reporting) estimator and its shot-noise
      correction.

  hivon02_master_mode_coupling_deconvolution:
    id: hivon02_master_mode_coupling_deconvolution
    claim: |
      MASTER describes the mode coupling from incomplete sky
      coverage analytically through the harmonic transform of the
      sky window and corrects for it to obtain an unbiased C_ℓ.
      Both estimators considered here decouple their bandpowers
      this way.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1086/338126"
        quote:
          exact: "The harmonic mode-mode coupling induced by the incomplete sky coverage is described analytically by the SHT of the sky window and corrected for in order to obtain an unbiased estimate of the"
        location:
          page: 2
    scope: |
      Hivon et al. 2002, ApJ 567, 2; derived for CMB temperature
      maps. NaMaster (Alonso et al. 2019) provides the spin-2
      implementation used here.

  alonso19_namaster_unbiased_spin2_pseudo_cl:
    id: alonso19_namaster_unbiased_spin2_pseudo_cl
    claim: |
      NaMaster provides a unified pseudo-Cℓ framework for any pair of
      spin-0 or spin-2 fields, and its validation suite recovers the
      input power spectra with no detectable bias in complex
      scenarios.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1093/mnras/stz093"
        quote:
          exact: "provides a unified framework to compute angular cross-power spectra of any pair of spin-0 or spin-2 fields"
        location:
          page: 1
      - id: ev2
        doi: "10.1093/mnras/stz093"
        quote:
          exact: "use it to show that the code is able to recover the input power spectra in the most complex scenarios with no detectable bias."
        location:
          page: 1
    scope: |
      Alonso, Sanchez & Slosar 2019, MNRAS 484, 4127; validated on
      maps, extended to catalogs by Wolz et al. 2025. Paper II uses
      it to decouple the bandpowers.

  reinecke23_sht_on_arbitrary_grids:
    id: reinecke23_sht_on_arbitrary_grids
    claim: |
      The `ducc` nonuniform-FFT code performs spherical harmonic
      transforms efficiently on completely arbitrary point sets,
      which is what makes evaluating spin-2 transforms directly at
      the tens of millions of UNIONS source positions practical.
    created_at: "2026-10-31T00:00:00Z"
    evidence:
      - id: ev1
        doi: "10.1051/0004-6361/202346717"
        quote:
          exact: "This publicly available code enables de facto efficient spherical harmonic transforms on completely arbitrary grids, and it might be applied in other areas as well."
        location:
          page: 1
    scope: |
      Reinecke, Belkner & Carron 2023, A&A 678, A165, motivated by
      CMB lensing; applied to catalog pseudo-Cℓ by Wolz et al. 2025.

texts.analyses/mocks/astra.yaml:
version: "0.0.14"
name: "GLASS mocks"
description: |
  The suite of 350 systematics-free GLASS lognormal realizations on
  which the covariances and null tests are validated, made here from the
  catalog footprint and the fiducial n(z), and measured with the same
  TreeCorr and NaMaster recipes as the data. Each realization samples
  unit-weight galaxies with input shears and Gaussian intrinsic
  ellipticities inside the footprint, at the density and σ_e the
  [suite](#decisions.mock_suite) sets: the fiducial catalog's
  weight-effective count and σ_e for the data-matched suite, or the
  published settings, whose density is 17% above the data's
  ([mocks_are_over_constraining](#../analyses.validation.analyses.glass_mocks.findings.mocks_are_over_constraining)).
  A realization is fixed by its seed, 1 000 000 plus its number, so the
  [summary of realization 00001](#outputs.glass_mock_realization_00001) is
  that of the catalog the suite measured. The footprint, density and σ_e come
  from the [catalog summary](#inputs.catalog_summary); no recipe here reads a
  data catalog.

inputs:
  - id: catalog_summary
    from: ../catalog_processing.catalog_summary

  - id: redshift_distributions
    from: ../redshift_distributions

outputs:
  - {id: glass_mock_sampling, from: generation.glass_mock_sampling}
  - {id: glass_mock_realization_00001, from: generation.glass_mock_realization_00001}

  - id: glass_mock_suite
    from: glass_suite.glass_suite_bundle

  - id: glass_mock_xi_fine
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      TreeCorr ξ_±(θ) of each realization on exactly the data's
      1000-bin integration grid, 0.5′–300′, with no response correction
      or leakage subtraction, since the realizations carry input shears
      and no PSF leakage. Stacked (`meanr`, `xip`, `xim`, `npairs`,
      `weight` per realization, with the mock IDs). Both
      configuration-space transforms of the mocks integrate over this
      grid.
    inputs: [glass_mock_suite]
    decisions: [mock_suite, integration_grid]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/glass_mock_suite.py --extract mock_xi_fine.npz
        --suite {inputs.glass_mock_suite} --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "4GB" }

  - id: glass_mock_xi_reporting
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      The same TreeCorr call on the 20-bin reporting grid, stacked in the
      layout of [glass_mock_xi_fine](#outputs.glass_mock_xi_fine). It
      defines the reporting bins of the pure-E/B transform, whose
      integrals run over the fine ξ_±.
    inputs: [glass_mock_suite]
    decisions: [mock_suite, reporting_binning]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/glass_mock_suite.py --extract mock_xi_reporting.npz
        --suite {inputs.glass_mock_suite} --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "4GB" }

  - id: glass_mock_cl
    type: data
    format: tar.gz
    description: |
      Catalog-based NaMaster Cℓ bandpowers of each realization, unweighted,
      on the data's 32 √ℓ-spaced bands over 8 ≤ ℓ ≤ 2048, one
      `cl_glass_mock_<id>_4096.npy` per realization (rows ℓ, EE, EB, BE,
      BB). Their BB row is every mock Cℓ^BB result: the harmonic column of
      the per-realization campaign, the Cℓ panels of the mock-validation
      figure, and the measured mock-to-data BB variance ratio.
    inputs: [glass_mock_suite]
    decisions: [mock_suite]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/glass_mock_suite.py --extract cl
        --suite {inputs.glass_mock_suite} --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 1, memory: "4GB" }

decisions:
  mock_suite:
    from: ../mock_suite
  fiducial_catalog:
    from: ../fiducial_catalog
  integration_grid:
    from: ../integration_grid
  reporting_binning:

texts.analyses/mocks/analyses/generation/astra:
version: "0.0.14"
name: "GLASS generation inputs"
description: |
  What every GLASS realization is drawn from: the galaxy density and shape
  dispersion they are sampled with, and the matter shell spectra the
  lognormal fields are drawn from; plus the summary of realization 00001, the
  one realization whose catalog a covariance reads. The footprint the
  galaxies are sampled in is the nside-4096 occupancy of the
  [suite](#decisions.mock_suite)'s footprint catalog in the
  [catalog summary](#inputs.catalog_summary): the v1.4.6 cut catalog for the
  published suite (2757.25 deg²), the fiducial catalog for the data-matched
  one.

inputs:
  - id: catalog_summary
    from: ../catalog_summary

  - id: redshift_distributions
    from: ../redshift_distributions

outputs:
  - id: glass_mock_sampling
    type: data
    format: json
    description: |
      The galaxy density (arcmin⁻²) and per-component intrinsic
      ellipticity dispersion every realization is sampled with. The
      published suite keeps its 6.0905 arcmin⁻² and 0.2684. The
      data-matched suite derives both from the fiducial catalog's summary:
      the density at which a realization's expected count on the footprint
      equals the catalog's weight-effective count (Σw)²/Σw², and
      σ_e² = Σw²(e₁² + e₂²)/(2Σw²), the definition behind the data
      covariance's shape noise, so that mocks and data carry the same shape
      noise.
    inputs: [catalog_summary, redshift_distributions]
    decisions: [mock_suite, fiducial_catalog]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/glass_mock_sampling.py
        --suite {decisions.mock_suite} --fiducial-catalog {decisions.fiducial_catalog}
        --summary {inputs.catalog_summary}
        --nz "$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py nz_file blind_a)"
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 2, memory: "16GB" }

  - id: glass_mock_shell_cls
    type: data
    format: npy
    description: |
      CAMB matter angular power spectra, non-Limber to ℓ = 4096, for every
      pair of the 32 linear-window shells (every 200 Mpc in comoving
      distance to z = 3), in the suite's cosmology. Every realization
      draws its lognormal matter fields from them.
    decisions: [mock_suite]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/glass_mock_shell_cls.py --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 64, memory: "64GB" }

  - id: glass_mock_realization_00001
    type: data
    format: npz
    description: |
      The catalog summary of realization 00001, its weighted count map and
      shape-noise sum in the layout of the
      [catalog summary](#inputs.catalog_summary): the window and noise of the
      Cℓ [reference covariance](#../../decisions.reference_covariance) under
      `mockmatched`. The catalog itself is discarded.
    inputs: [catalog_summary, glass_mock_shell_cls, glass_mock_sampling, redshift_distributions]
    decisions: [mock_suite, fiducial_catalog]
    recipe:
      command: >
        python src/workflow/scripts/glass_mock_summary.py --number 1 --key SP_v1.4.6.3_glass_mock_v2
        --summary {inputs.catalog_summary}
        --suite {decisions.mock_suite} --fiducial-catalog {decisions.fiducial_catalog}
        --shell-cls {inputs.glass_mock_shell_cls} --sampling {inputs.glass_mock_sampling}
        --nz "$(python src/workflow/scripts/decision_values.py nz_file blind_a)"
        --out-file {output}
      resources: { cpus: 16, memory: "48GB" }

decisions:
  mock_suite:
    from: ../mock_suite
  fiducial_catalog:
    from: ../fiducial_catalog
